When Captain America lifts Mjolnir and shouts "Avengers, assemble!", it serves as a direct callback to a similar moment in the comics' Fear Itself #7, where Steve Rogers wields Thor's hammer and rallies the heroes with the same battle cry.
Mantis assumes a martial arts stance during the final battle; this is a reference to her portrayal as a skilled martial artist in the comics.

Spider-Man appears noticeably flustered when he first meets Captain Marvel. This is a subtle nod to the occasional romantic ship tease between the two characters in the comics, where they are closer in age and have had flirtatious moments, including going on a date. In the final battle, when Peter worries that Captain Marvel won't be able to reach the Quantum Tunnel with the Infinity Gauntlet, several female heroes (including Scarlet Witch, Okoye, the Wasp, Rescue, Valkyrie, Shuri, Gamora, Nebula, and Mantis) join together to help clear a path for her. This sequence serves as a nod to the all-female superhero team A-Force, which was first introduced in the 2015 Secret Wars event, as well as to the Lady Liberators (also known as the Liberators), an earlier all-female team that debuted in The Avengers #83.

Captain Marvel proving to be a physical match for Thanos during their confrontation in the final battle is a subtle nod to the original Captain Marvel, Mar-Vell and Thanos being longstanding bitter foes in the comics, most notably during the "Thanos War" storyline in Captain Marvel #25–#34.

When Thor joins the Guardians of the Galaxy, he jokingly suggests renaming the team the "Asgardians of the Galaxy." This is a reference to the comic book team of the same name, formed by Asgardian characters to protect the galaxy after the original Guardians of the Galaxy disbanded following the Infinity Countdown event.

At the end of the film, an elderly Steve Rogers names Sam Wilson the new Captain America, a moment that also happened in the comics. However, in the comics, Rogers' Super Soldier Serum was drained, causing him to age greatly until becoming old. In the MCU, he aged naturally after time-traveling back to the 1949, before returning to 2023 to name Wilson as his successor; Rogers' appearing in the present as an old man after living several decades following WWII borrows elements from Ultimates #3, where Bucky Barnes' Ultimate Marvel counterpart appeared in the present as an old man as unlike his mainstream counterpart he was not killed in WWII (which this issue was released before the Winter Soldier was introduced in the mainstream universe); Rogers' living a quiet life with Peggy Carter borrows several elements from the House of M event, where Rogers lives a married life with Peggy in the past instead of being a superhero.

In the five-year jump between the Ambush on Thanos and the Time Heist, Bruce Banner combined his human and Hulk personalities, an event inspired by the comics, in which Banner and his Green and Grey Hulk personas seemingly combined into one, creating the "Professor Hulk" persona.
Hawkeye's becoming a violent vigilante after his family dies mirrors the events of the Ultimates 3, where he changes costume and becomes far darker, after the same thing happened to him.
The territory of "New Asgard" is based on the Asgard built by Thor during J. Michael Straczynski's run. Just like in the movie, the comics' New Asgard was built after the events of Ragnarök.
Tony's line "you mess with time, it tends to mess back" is quite similar to what he told to Wolverine and Invisible Woman during the comic event, "Age of Ultron".

Precedent for Thor dual wielding Stormbreaker and Mjølnir includes Jason Aaron's The God Butcher/Godbomb, where he wields the hammers of his present and future self, and Johnathan Hickman's Avengers run, where he used Stormbreaker and an alternate version of Mjølnir.
Hulk forming a Friendship with Rocket, references how Rocket first appeared in an Incredible Hulk comic.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Avengers: Endgame is the culmination of the first 22 films of the Marvel Cinematic Universe that comprise The Infinity Saga.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The Avengers travel to the events and/or locations of the following films: Captain America, Iron Man, Hulk and Ant-Man travel to the Battle of New York from The Avengers. The scene with the circle shot in which the Avengers assembled for the first time is featured again. During this sequence, Hulk travels to the New York Sanctum, which was featured in Doctor Strange; Thor and Rocket travel to the events of Thor: The Dark World; War Machine and Nebula travel to the events of Guardians of the Galaxy. The scene in which Star-Lord dances on Morag is featured again, but this time through War Machine and Nebula's perspective; Captain America and Iron Man travel to Camp Lehigh, which was featured in Captain America: The First Avenger and Captain America: The Winter Soldier; Black Widow and Hawkeye travel to Vormir, which was featured in Avengers: Infinity War.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Avengers: Endgame is the first Marvel Studios production to feature a MCU character originating from a Marvel Television production, featuring an alternate Edwin Jarvis from Agent Carter, with James D'Arcy reprising the role. Unrealized dialogue from the screenplay featured Jarvis mentioning that he would teach Tony Stark the fundamentals of Judo. In the second episode of the second season of Agent Carter, Jarvis endeavored to learn Judo following his experience with Peggy Carter; Previously, the lead characters of MCU's Netflix series Defenders were in consideration during early drafts of Avengers: Infinity War.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The Mexican Cartel, which first appeared in the second season of Marvel's Daredevil and later in The Punisher, is mentioned.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: During the Theft of the Time Stone, the Ancient One mentions that Stephen Strange is currently performing a surgery. Strange's former workplace is Metropolitan General Hospital, a hospital franchise first introduced in Daredevil.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: This is the first MCU movie in which all of the current leading heroes of their respective series appeared.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: During the scene where Tony Stark and Scott Lang attempt to steal the Tesseract in alternate timeline 2012, the former mentions that Brock Rumlow and Jasper Sitwell are undercover Hydra agents working within S.H.I.E.L.D., referencing the events of Captain America: The Winter Soldier.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: While talking to the Avengers about the Aether, Thor mentions the events of Thor: The Dark World.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: While arriving at New Asgard, Hulk reminds Rocket that the Asgardians lost their home, as seen in Thor: Ragnarok.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Right before appearing at the Battle of Earth, Sam Wilson says to Captain America through the radio "On your left," a reference to Captain America: The Winter Soldier.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The briefing on the Infinity Stones has Hulk eating the "Hunka-Hulka Burning Fudge" Ben & Jerry's ice cream mentioned in Avengers: Infinity War. The brand helped with the product placement, but denied that said flavor would eventually be sold.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: During the Battle of Earth, Black Panther calls Hawkeye "Clint!", a reference to the fight between the two during the Battle at Leipzig-Halle Airport, as seen in Captain America: Civil War. When Captain America throws Mjølnir to Spider-Man, he calls Spider-Man "Queens," a reference to their meeting during the Battle at Leipzig-Halle Airport.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: During Tony Stark's funeral, his original Arc Reactor from Iron Man can be seen.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When Morgan Stark says that she wants to eat a cheeseburger to Happy Hogan, Hogan says that her father liked cheeseburgers, alluding to Iron Man.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Right before traveling to the past, Steve Rogers tells Bucky Barnes not to "do anything stupid until [he gets] back", to which Barnes says "How can [he]. Taking all the stupid with [Rogers]", a reference to a conversation between them in Captain America: The First Avenger.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: This is the first film where Iron Man and Captain America see each other since Captain America: Civil War.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: This is the first film where Iron Man and Thor see each other since Avengers: Age of Ultron.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: This is the first film to feature both War Machine and Happy Hogan since Iron Man 3.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: This is the first time Star-Lord visits Earth in 35 years since 1988. Additionally, this is also the first time most of the Guardians of the Galaxy (except Rocket and Groot) ever visit Earth.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Captain America is seen wearing his Stealth Uniform for the first time since Captain America: The Winter Soldier.

facts.section: Other Works that Reference Avengers: Endgame
facts.text: In Spider-Man/Deadpool Vol 1 #50: The Manipulator: Part 3, Spider-Man and Deadpool arrive into the "real world" and see a billboard advertising Avengers: Endgame using the logo of the film.

Avengers: Endgame is the first movie in the MCU to not have any mid-credits or post-credits scenes. After the credits, as the Marvel Studios logo is displayed on the screen the sound of a clanging can be heard, representing Tony Stark making his first suit during the events of Iron Man; This is also the first movie in the MCU to be re-released in the theaters.

Katherine Langford was announced to have a role in Avengers: Endgame. However, she did not appear in the film. In an interview, the Russo Brothers revealed that Langford's role would be the teenage version of Morgan Stark and that her scene would have occurred after Tony snapped his fingers.
The signing of actors' names in the end credits was an homage to the ending of Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country.
During the Marvel Studios logo animation, all images of characters killed in the Snap in the previous film have been removed. Despite having survived the Snap, Ant-Man was removed as well.
Avengers: Endgame is the first ever film to cross a billion dollars on its opening weekend.
Director Joe Russo and Jim Starlin, the creator of Thanos, both have a cameo during the consultation session organized by Steve Rogers.

Korg is seen playing Fortnite, in which Thanos appears as a playable character when a player obtains an Infinity Gauntlet. Later, in an update to promote Avengers: Endgame, Fortnite added weapons like Iron Man's repulsors, Thor's Stormbreaker, Captain America's Shield, and Hawkeye's bow; Fortnite actually had a crossover with Marvel to mark the theatrical release of Avengers: Infinity War. The crossover was called "Infinity Gauntlet". Players could transform into Thanos by finding the Infinity Gauntlet that landed at a random spot at the start of the game. If Thanos was eliminated, the gauntlet would fall to the ground, free for any other character to collect. The crossover ended on 15th May 2018; The film depicted the current season to be Season 5 as of October, 2023. In November, 2023, Fortnite released Chapter 4: Season OG, where for 1 month, players were back on the Fortnite Chapter 1 map, coincidentally starting with Season 5; Korg is seen wearing a Hawaiian-style shirt with art of pineapples on it, a shirt his actor Taika Waititi is known for wearing in public.
Avengers: Endgame is the second sequel film to be in the same Phase as its predecessor, following Iron Man 2 and carrying on with Spider-Man: Far From Home.

Avengers: Endgame marks the final acting performances of Lee Moore, who passed away on August 16, 2018 a year prior to the film's release and Robert Redford, who had retired from acting prior to the film's release which was released after the film The Old Man & the Gun which he intended to be his final film performance. The film also marks the final appearance of Stan Lee in a Marvel Studios production and Marvel Cinematic Universe film being the second and last to be released posthumously after he also passed away on November 12, 2018.
With a running time of 3 hours and 1 minute, Avengers: Endgame is the longest Marvel and Disney produced film. It also broke The Dark Knight Rises' 165 minute runtime of the longest superhero movie.
Avengers: Endgame is the highest-grossing film of all time, surpassing Avatar, which was number 1 for almost 10 years.
Avengers: Endgame is the first film to be the highest-grossing film of all time at the time of its release that didn't win an Oscar.
During the final battle, there were supposed to be two reunion scenes similar to Tony and Parker's between Rocket and Groot, and Scott and Hope respectively.
The film came out on the 80th anniversary of Marvel comics.
This was Chadwick Boseman’s final role as Black Panther prior to his death on August 28, 2020.
This film is the only Marvel Cinematic Universe film on Disney+ to be fully available in IMAX Enhanced.

While Scott Lang was trapped in the Quantum Realm for five years, a rat accidentally stepped on the button of Luis' van's quantum tunnel controls, freeing him and enabling his return to the main timeline. This improbable event allowed Scott to propose the time heist plan to the Avengers, setting the events of the film in motion. Co-director Joe Russo jokingly referred to the rat as the true hero who saved the universe in a 2019 interview with Chinese site QQ, stating: "Yes, the mouse saved the universe!". Fans have humorously speculated that the rat was a meta-reference to Mickey Mouse, the mascot of The Walt Disney Company (which acquired Marvel Entertainment in 2009), as if Disney's iconic character symbolically "saved" the billion-dollar MCU franchise.
Characters from the comics adapted for the movie are Corvus Glaive, Cull Obsidian, Ebony Maw, Proxima Midnight, and Eitri.
The movie also makes the debut of three Marvel Comics locations. These are the planets Vormir, Nidavellir, and Titan.
The movie's name is a reference to the The Infinity War story-arc. The movie also took inspiration from other Thanos-centric storylines such as Infinity Gauntlet, Thanos Quest, and Infinity.
The invasion of Wakanda by Thanos' forces, the Outriders, mirrors the invasion of Wakanda in the Infinity event.
The movie also references comics characters such as Morgan Stark, A'Lars, and Captain Marvel.
Ebony Maw uses a line from Mephisto in the The Infinity Gauntlet storyline and his role as someone who advises Thanos in his choices while being devoted to him mirrors that of Mephisto's.
Thanos tortures Mantis and Drax in a similar fashion to the way he does to Starfox and Nebula in the Infinity Gauntlet.
Spider-Man shoots a web to Thanos' face, just as Peter did in the Infinity Gauntlet.
Despite not being from the comics, Thanos uses bubbles, as he does in Capcom’s Marvel fighting game series Marvel vs. Capcom: Infinite.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: This is the fourth appearance of the Infinity Gauntlet, the third being Thor: Ragnarok, the second being Avengers: Age of Ultron, and the first being Thor, though the one in Thor and Thor: Ragnarok is a replica and not the real gauntlet.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: This is Thanos' fourth appearance overall, the third being Avengers: Age of Ultron, the second being Guardians of the Galaxy and the first being The Avengers. This is also the first movie where Josh Brolin is credited as Thanos as his last two appearances as the character were uncredited.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Despite not appearing on the film, Ant-Man and Hawkeye are mentioned as being under house arrest due to the events of Captain America: Civil War.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: While talking with his fiancée, Pepper Potts, Tony Stark mentions that he put himself in a surgery to get out his Arc Reactor, as seen in Iron Man 3.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Thor references various events in his filmography. These include: the Battle of New York, the Death of Frigga, the Death of Odin, Hela's Assault on Asgard, among others.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Members of the Guardians of the Galaxy also allude to events on their film series, such as the ending dance-off from their first outing, and their battle with Ego in Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Iron Man also references the events of Spider-Man: Homecoming when nagging Spider-Man.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Loki quotes Tony Stark's ""We have a Hulk." line from The Avengers to Thanos.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The post-credits caption promises "Thanos will return".

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: This is the first film to feature both War Machine and Pepper Potts onscreen together since Iron Man 3.

A short, blue-skinned alien is spotted in the Collector's Museum on Knowhere. This is a visual reference to Tobias Fünke, portrayed by David Cross, from the TV series Arrested Development, which had episodes directed by the Russo Brothers.
Star-Lord calls Thanos Grimace, referencing the purple character from McDonald's.

Iron Man calls Ebony Maw Squidward, a SpongeBob SquarePants character. He also nicknames Star-Lord as Flash Gordon, a space opera hero seen in comic strips and film series; He also nicknames Drax as Mr. Clean.

It is revealed that ice cream brand Ben and Jerry's made flavors named after both Iron Man (Stark Raving Hazelnuts) and Hulk (Hunka-Hulka Burning Fudge). The Hulk is even seen eating his flavor in Avengers: Endgame. When questioned whether they would sell such flavors, Ben & Jerry had to deny it.
Spider-Man bases his plan on the death of the Xenomorph Queen from Aliens. He also refers to the aliens bursting from the chest from the Alien franchise.
Tony Stark asked Doctor Strange what his other job is besides making balloon animals, referencing a skit from Jimmy Kimmel Live, where he does balloon animals for a birthday party.
This is the first film in which Spider-Man is shown punching someone, as he was seen throwing a punch at Thanos during the Battle of Titan.
Avengers: Infinity War is the only Avengers film to not feature all of the original Avengers in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, as Hawkeye does not appear.
The movie was released on the 55th anniversaries of both Iron Man and Doctor Strange.
The film's poster was seen in the 20th Century Studios film Free Guy.

According to the movie's writers Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely, when putting together the casts for both Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame, they made baseball cards of all of the characters that were alive within the movies and put them on two walls. One wall was for Avengers: Infinity War and the other was for the sequel. They also stated that everyone from the main heroes down to minor characters, such as Ian Boothby, were considered for appearing in the movie.

Avengers: Infinity War was originally titled Avengers: Infinity War - Part I, with Avengers: Endgame being titled Avengers: Infinity War - Part II. However, due to to the movies being different from each other, Marvel decided to rename the movies.

The teaser poster for the film was revealed by Tom Holland during a live Instagram post as a spoof on his (along with fellow cast member, Mark Ruffalo) previous instances of accidentally revealing key details of Marvel projects.

Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely said that they considered including Daredevil and Luke Cage from the Netflix shows in small cameos but it was dropped as they felt that their appearances would be nothing more than a "glorified cameo" and deemed it impossible to keep with the showrunners.
The director of the first Thor film, Kenneth Branagh, provides the voice to the distress call of the Asgardian ship in the opening credits.

This film sees the return of the character Red Skull. Following the character's supposed death in Captain America: The First Avenger, many fans speculated he actually didn't die and was instead transported somewhere and long speculated about his possible return. Interviews with Kevin Feige and Hugo Weaving teased this, but there was never anything concrete. Finally, the character returns in this film, with his appearance being kept a top secret until the film's release.

Characters including Howard the Duck, Sharon Carter, Bor, and Happy Hogan were included in early versions of the movie, but they were ultimately removed. Happy Hogan's appearance can be seen in one of the film's deleted scenes.

The Wakandan's war chant scene was improvised by the actors, the Russo brothers did not think of the scene because they haven't seen Black Panther by the time they were writing the script, but they really liked it and decided to keep it in the final version. The chant, "Yibambe", is Xhosa for "Resist".
The title and event of "Secret Wars" is based off of the event in Marvel Comics.
The film has been delayed three times, from November 7, 2025 to May 1, 2026 to May 7, 2027 to December 17th, 2027.
The film is the sixth film in the Avengers franchise, marking the longest franchise in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
In a theater PSA for the film Deadpool & Wolverine, Deadpool talks about Secret Wars to Wolverine before being cut off by a phone ringtone.
Characters from the comics adapted from the movie in the main cast are Erik Killmonger, Nakia, Okoye, Shuri, Ramonda, Zuri, M'Baku, and W'Kabi.
The movie also features locations such as Birnin Zana, Jabari Village, Warrior Falls, and Djalia, from the Black Panther comic books.
One of the lines that T'Challa utters to Klaue "every breath you take is mercy from me" was used in New Avengers #22.
T'Challa facing a rhinoceros was taken from Jungle Action #9.
Killmonger becoming a version of the Black Panther, has precedence in Marvel comics history.

Ryan Coogler brought in consultants who are experts on African history and politics to work on defining Wakanda: "There are many African countries, each with different histories, mythologies, and cultures; there are several tribes who live amongst each other, and together they make the identity of their country. We honed in on some of the history/cultural influences from African countries and then made estimations."
The filmmakers cite The Godfather films and the James Bond films as an influence on the story, calling it "a big, operatic family drama centered on a world of international espionage".
Daniel Kaluuya described Black Panther as "Marvel's Game of Thrones."
Production designer Hannah Beachler mentioned Blade Runner as one the main source of inspiration for Wakanda's futuristic design.

Ryan Coogler describe the film's central theme as responsibility and identity: "What do the powerful owe those in need? It separates the good-guys from the villains. What value is strength unless you're using it to help someone? Wakanda pretends to be just another struggling African country, but some of its neighbours are struggling for real. If Wakandans don't stand up for themselves, who will? But if they stand only for themselves, then who are they?"
Ryan Coogler and Joe Robert Cole considered the possibility of introducing Eli Bradley in the film, but they ultimately dropped the idea in favor of focusing on Wakandan characters more.
Ryan Coogler wished to add Spider-Man villain Kraven the Hunter to the movie, though due to legal issues regarding the deal with Sony, he couldn't feature him.

Black Panther was the first of the Marvel characters whose movie rights reverted to Marvel, having been previously owned by Artisan Entertainment, Columbia Pictures, and 20th Century Fox. Marvel Studios got the rights back in 2005. The character almost had a film in the 90's starring Wesley Snipes; The character would have been in the third or fourth Fantastic Four film directed by Tim Story, and was considered to be played by Djimon Hounsou.
Black Panther is stated to be "very honest and gritty" film by Michael B. Jordan (the actor who portrays Erik Killmonger) unlike other MCU films.

Black Panther is the first MCU film since Captain America: Civil War to include a prologue scene ahead of any studio logos, though Spider-Man: Homecoming included one between the Sony logos and the Marvel Studios logo.
The post-credits caption promises "Black Panther will return in Avengers: Infinity War".

Black Panther is one of the only four MCU films not featuring Iron Man (along with Captain Marvel, Spider-Man: Far From Home, Spider-Man: No Way Home and Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness) that grossed $1 billion and $900 million worldwide.

Black Panther was credited with helping to save the life of Xavier Cunningham, an eleven-year-old boy who was impaled on a barbecue skewer following a fall from his treehouse; Xavier stated he knew not to remove the skewer as he remembered that Erik Killmonger died only after removing the spear he'd been stabbed with.

On November 29, 2020, the Marvel Studios logo animation on the Disney+ version of the film was replaced with a tribute to Chadwick Boseman, similar to the one for Stan Lee in Captain Marvel. Boseman would have turned 44 on that date.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When Namora offers Shuri some clothes, Riri Williams remarks at how that trope is present in many movies. Shuri responds that Williams should see what she had to wear at Warrior Falls, which is a callback to Shuri's joke in Black Panther where she acts like she is challenging for the throne, but just complains about her corset.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: In the screenplay, Shuri guesses that Riri Williams either works for DARPA, Roxxon Corporation, or Project P.E.G.A.S.U.S.
In the comics, Namor and the rest of his kingdom are Atlanteans. However, in the film, they are Talokanil. This was done to avoid similarities with Aquaman in the DCEU.
The Midnight Angel Armor closely resembles the Dora Milaje's current uniform in the comics.
When analyzing Namor, Shuri claims him to be as strong as the Hulk, a clear nod to Hulk and Namor's frequent fights in the comics.
During his final confrontation with Shuri, Namor says "Imperious Rex" in Yucatec, which in the comics is his main battle cry.

According to Ryan Coogler, the original script was different from the released script as it was written before the tragic death of Chadwick Boseman. It would have followed T'Challa, who was struggling after a five-year absence due to the Blip. T'Challa II would have been shown earlier in the film as T'Challa struggled to cope with the fact that he missed five years of his son's life. Additionally, Namor was still supposed to be the villain.
In the subtitles of the movie, different languages are displayed in different colors. Yucatec-Mayan is in blue, Xhosa is in yellow, and Spanish is in white.
The phrase "This Jade Tooth Bites" is engraved on the Megalodon jawbone used by Namor as his throne.
The film marks the MCU debuts of Yelena Belova, Alexei Shostakov/Red Guardian, Melina Vostokoff/Iron Maiden, Rick Mason and Taskmaster.
During their conversation in Melina's house, Yelena mistakenly refers to Alexei as the "Crimson Dynamo," the name of an Iron Man supervillain in the comics.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On November 8, 2020, Scarlett confirmed that the film would finally address what happened in Budapest, which was first teased back in 2012's The Avengers in a conversation that Black Widow and Hawkeye had.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On November 9, 2020, David Harbour teased that Natasha and Alexei have been working together on and off since the 1990's as their bonds have strengthened with each other. Harbour also revealed how close his character is with Nat, once rescuing her from the Red Room but later throwing her back into the fire.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On November 16, 2020, it was mentioned that because the film is set between the events of Captain America: Civil War and Avengers: Infinity War, Black Widow will find herself without the support of S.H.I.E.L.D. or the Avengers, Black Widow will have to get supplies and vehicles for her mission through O.T. Fagbenle's Rick Mason.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On November 30, 2020, reports began to circulate that Florence Pugh has reportedly join the cast of Hawkeye.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On February 2, 2021, Jac Schaeffer, who serves as the head writer and creator of WandaVision, says it was more of a challenge to write the Black Widow film, which she also was part of the team, than Marvel's first series.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On February 16, 2021 it was revealed that Chloé Zhao, who is directing and did some writing for the Eternals film, was at one time, in the running for directing the Black Widow film.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On March 1, 2021, storyboards for WandaVision, which featured a Black Widow reference were leaked. It specifically referenced Black Widow's death and lack of funeral to honor her at the end of Avengers: Endgame.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On April 28, 2021, a new featurette released by Marvel in celebration of National Superhero Day for the Black Widow film was released on this day with Scarlett Johansson asking the audience how much they know about her Black Widow character.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On May 13, 2021, it was revealed that a current release in theaters remains unclear and would likely be impacted one way or the other by how films like Black Widow and Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings do.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On June 16, 2021, Scarlett mention in an interview that she had been waiting for Marvel boss Kevin Feige to green-light a solo film since The Avengers rocked the box office in 2012. However, she further revealed that she was glad the film didn't come into fruition until recently, as it would have been a very different movie that the final version audiences will see on July 9, 2021. Also on this day, Scarlett also mentioned how proud she felt that her character of Black Widow has evolved from being hyper sexualized all the way back in Iron Man 2, to a more evolved and fully developed Natasha in her standalone film.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On June 15, 2021, a promotional video for Yelena Belova was released by Marvel Studios.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On June 19, 2021, Kevin Feige said that "exploring the past, present, and future of the MCU is certainly in the cards" during a recent press conference. Which hints at Black Widow film not be the only prequel the MCU may have in store for audiences.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On July 3, 2021, Shortland hinted that the Black Widow film franchise could continue with a sequel revolving around a different character.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On July 7, 2021, it was announced that Disney's Marvel Studios films and MCU series won’t be putting in an appearance during the virtual edition of Comic-Con @ Home.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On July 9, 2021, the post-credits scene has Yelena Belova being approached by Contessa Valentina Allegra de Fontaine who previously appeared last in The Falcon and The Winter Soldier. Moreover, it appears that Yelena has been carrying out missions for the Contessa, with her latest target being none other than Hawkeye. Which in turn sets up Florence Pugh's confirmed appearance on Hawkeye.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On October 6, 2021, it was revealed that while Marvel’s What If...? season 1 has just concluded, the creative team behind What If…? teased that for the second season, Head writer A.C. Bradley said that “Going into the second season, we're sticking with anthology form, and it's going to be all-new stories, lots of fun, new heroes, and pulling more from Phase Four than we were obviously able to this season. Hopefully, we'll see hints of the Eternals and Shang-Chi and the Black Widow film characters too.
Black Widow is the third film to be set as a prequel (the first being Captain America: The First Avenger and the second Captain Marvel).
This is the first female-led solo film to open a Phase (4) in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
This is the first solo film centered around a character who is deceased in the current MCU timeline.
This is the second female led superhero film from Marvel Cinematic Universe after Captain Marvel.

The film was released on July 9, 2021, making the longest gap between two films since The Incredible Hulk and Iron Man 2, as Spider-Man: Far From Home was released on July 2, 2019, making a gap of over 24 months between Black Widow and Far From Home. It also marks the longest gap between the last film of an MCU phase and the first film in another phase.

On October 7, 2020, it was revealed that Disney and McDonald’s have teamed up to offer a new collection of Marvel Studio toys as part of the McDonald Happy Meals.The line up will feature the likes of Falcon, Winter Soldier, Wanda Maximoff, Vision, Groot, Hulkbuster, Wasp, Hulk and the Black Widow herself. This merchandise of toys is also tied to promotion for WandaVision and The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, two Disney+ shows that premiered in January and March 2021, respectively.

On October 18, 2020, Dan Loeb, the hedge fund manager for Third Point, suggested having high-profile releases on Disney+ instead. His argument laid in Disney+ needing to attract more subscribers with more content, otherwise they would always be in Netflix's shadow; Loeb placed a $1 billion stake in the company. Thus, he believes that the only way to keep the story going is to release Black Widow on the streaming site instead.

On November 5, 2020, several new images from the recently released book, Marvel's Black Widow: The Official Movie Special appeared online and gave a glimpse actor O-T Fagbenle's somewhat mysterious character Rick Mason. This was further expanded when O-T Fagbenle himself said on Black Widow: The Official Movie Special Book that "Mason is a finder for people who aren't so affiliated with armies, like people who are part of the underworld. He can find anything you need as well. He's had a relationship doing that work for the Black Widow, and they have a bit of a vibe going on. There's a sense that there's more to their relationship than it being purely work-related, so that's always in the mix"
On November 9, 2020, Epic Games teased that the next Marvel skin that would be available for free in the subsequent Marvel Knockout Series cup would be the Snowsuit Black Widow skin.

On November 16, 2020, Ray Winstone shared some insight into the man in charge of the Red Room as well as his ties to David Harbour's Red Guardian. Winstone started off by saying in the Black Widow: The Official Movie Special that Dreykov is "a guy who came out of old Russia after the breakdown of communism. He really wanted to change something and wanted to protect his nation."; He elaborated further by saying how he thinks that Dreykov likely "was a man who started off with great intentions, but like most great men who are put into a situation, the greed and the power takes over. The Black Widow program is his. The Widows are part of his team. They're his ninjas."; As for what connection he has with Russia's version of Captain America, Winstone explains that "The Red Guardian was created as a Captain America, but a Russian version. He's a big powerful dude, who certainly started off believing in Russia. So, if America is making a bomb, then Russia has got to make a bigger bomb. Well, you have Captain America, who is s quite a good-looking guy. And he has got all the gear."

On December 15, 2020, news began to circulate that Marvel Studios is beginning to explore new talent deals to provide flexibility in case the pandemic or other factors lead the studio to bypass theaters and take the films straight to Disney+. This would mean that under the new contract language, key above-the-line talent like actors, writers, directors and producers will receive adjusted compensation depending on whether the film opens in theaters or debuts on the Disney+ streaming service.

On December 23, 2020 it was revealed through a release on Weibo, Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige announced that a Marvel-themed musical that would premiere on Bilibili (a Chinese video-sharing website) on December 31,2020 to celebrate the new year and what the MCU has in store for Phase 4.

On December 27, 2021, Patty Jenkins who has directed Wonder Woman and Wonder Woman 1984 for the DCEU respectively, revealed via social media that she'd relish the chance to helm more superhero movies in the coming years. When asked which franchise she'd choose if she had the choice, Patty said on Twitter: "Thank you for the question. Probably Superman, Spiderman or Black Widow! So much potential with all of them..."

On January 3, 2021, Milla Jovovich gushed about her daughter, who was cast as a young Natasha, and made everyone cry on set while filming Black Widow. Jovovich went onto say that, "We call her Baby Widow. She's such a fan of the Marvel movies and you know, Ever is just such an incredible talent. She's just a real natural and it was so wonderful to watch her on set...I mean, literally, she had everybody crying during one of her scenes! She's amazing. I think people are going to be really, really impressed when they see the movie next year."

On January 18, 2021, Kevin Feige would go on to acknowledge the unexpected similarities between The Blip and the COVID-19 pandemic, before reiterating that he wants any future references to Thanos' attack to "have more meaning behind it". As a result, Phase Four, would instead be focused on setting up new stories rather than looking back to past events.

On February 24, 2021, Disney President of Marketing Asad Ayaz discussed the promotional plan for Black Widow after the film's prolonged delay. When it was pointed out that Disney hasn't restarted the promotion for the movie ever since the shift in schedule, Ayaz shared that the last thing that they want to do in this situation is to overmarket the marketing campaign for the MCU prequel. However, Ayaz did reveal that his team will be introducing original materials when the marketing for Black Widow restarts as it gears up for its theatrical debut in May 2021. It was also unveiled that Disney will be taking a fresh approach in terms of selling the movie to viewers.

On February 25, 2021, Tom Holland revealed that Marvel still hasn't let him see the Black Widow film and it isn't for a lack of trying on his part. He mentioned how he has asked to view the film, bothering Marvel in recent weeks in the hopes they'll set up a screening. But Marvel has yet to do so and Holland finishes by calling out to Marvel in the hopes that, if they're listening, they'll finally let him see the film.
On February 26, 2021, makeup artist Deborah La Mia Denaver shared a behind-the-scenes look of the actress in the midst of an action sequence.

On March 1, 2021, in a new post from the Hasbro Pulse Facebook page confirmed two new Marvel Legends action figures going into production. These figures are for David Harbour's Red Guardian and Rachel Weisz's Melina Vostokoff from Marvel Studios' Black Widow.

On March 5, 2021, Black Widow makeup artist Deborah Lamia Denaver posted a new photo of Scarlet Johansson behind the scenes of the standalone film on her Instagram page. In it, Johansson seems to be getting touch-ups in between takes, fully decked out in the new black suit she will don.

On March 9, 2021, Florence Pugh released two behind the scenes stills of her with Scarlett in their costumes for the Black Widow film. Also on this day, it was reported at Disney’s annual shareholder meeting by CEO Bob Chapek continued to underscore that the release date for Marvel’s long-awaited feature Black Widow is May 7 will stick and that will be seen in theaters. Chapek made the same confirmation back on Feb. 11 during the studio’s fiscal Q1 earnings call.

On March 13, 2021 that Marvel Studios Assembled, will also be used that this documentary type series will be utilized for a behind-the-scenes look at Marvel Studios' first film of Phase 4, Black Widow, specifically mentioning the film's star Scarlett Johansson.
On March 14, 2021, some never before seen behind the scene images for the film were revealed via Twitter.

On March 19, 2021, several Black Widow-themed designs have been featured on boards around the Avengers Campus section of Disneyland's California Adventure.One features the logo of the upcoming movie on top of a metallic background, while another reads "Red Guardian" and features the character's symbol.

On March 23, 2021, it was revealed that because the end of the UK lockdown is currently scheduled to allow cinemas to reopen on May 17, some studio releases in May and June will now premiere over the summer. One such example was the announcement that Black Widow will move back to July and will be available simultaneously in cinemas and on Disney Plus.
On April 3, 2021, it began to be reported that allegedly, Cinema owners oppose Walt Disney Studios' decision to release Marvel films at the movies and on the streaming service simultaneously.

On April 5, 2021, it was revealed that the latest trailer for the film scored more than 70 million viewers in its first 24 hours, surpassing the second trailer by a substantial margin, of more than 13 million views. In addition, the previous spot for the superhero pic earned 57 million views in its first day.
On April 7, 2021, it was announced the Black Widow would be released simultaneously in Australian theaters and on Disney+ with Premier Access on July 9th, 2021 (just like in the USA).
On April 8, 2021, The film is rated PG-13 "for intense sequences of violence/action, some language and thematic material".
As of April 10, 2021, Disney+ has officially added the Premier Access preview page for the Black Widow film to its service in anticipation of its release on July 9, 2021.
On April 11, 2021, new merchandise in the form of a new Loungefly Black Widow backpack and two Taskmaster T-shirts have arrived at Disneyland Resort in advance of the film's premiere.
On April 25, 2021, it was revealed that the film is officially rated PG-13.
On April 29, 2021, O-T Fagbenle praised his co-star, Florence Pugh's performance in the film.

On April 30, 2021, The official Instagram page for the film posted a video promoting Marvel Studios' Black Widow featuring Rachel Weisz who is playing the character of Melina Vostokoff. The video includes Russian subtitles, which presumably means this is from one of Marvel's social media accounts promoting the film in Russia.
On May 3, 2021, Marvel debuted new footage from Black Widow teasing Natasha Romanoff's unfinished business in her solo film.
On May 4, 2021, a new promotional image featuring Taskmaster and Black Widow was released to the public.

On May 13, 2021, it was revealed that in spite of the many delays in the film, Black Widow’s director Cate Shortland mentioned how it’s been more than a year since the movie was fully finished, and that it has remained untouched since.

On May 24, 2021, Disney CEO Bob Chapek said the company made “the right call” by planning to release Black Widow in theaters the summer of 2021 at the same time it hits Disney+ as a Premier Access title.

On May 28, 2021 in an interview with Total Film Scarlett Johansson herself said in this interview that "Our goal was for [fans] to feel satisfied with this story; that they could maybe have some resolution, I think, with this character's death, in a way. It felt like people wanted that." Also on this day O.T. Fagbenle hinted that his character in 'Black Widow' is similar to that of Q in the 'James Bond' films.

On June 7, 2021, a promotional poster for IMAX theater was revealed, along with the information that for those that choosing to see the film in IMAX theaters, IMAX audiences will get to see over 20 minutes of footage in the expanded aspect ratio that the company is known for.
As of June 11, 2021, pre-sale tickets became available on Fandango for the Black Widow film. Also on this day,Taskmaster trended online after the Black Widow villain got their own emoji on Twitter.

On June 12, 2021, it was revealed that Marvel's Black Widow would become available to all Disney+ subscribers on October 6, 2021. This came three months after its theatrical release, and it's available on Disney+ starting July 9, 2021 with Premiere Access for those who pay the $29.99 price tag.

On June 25, 2021, Scarlett Johansson, whose husband is Saturday Night Live Weekend Update coanchor Colin Jost, only wanted limited details about her days filming Marvel's Black Widow when she came home. She further revealed that he refused to run lines with her, cause he didn't want to spoil himself with details from the script.

On June 28, 2021, Scarlett mentioned how she is proud that her character is going out on a high note with her standalone film. However, she admits it is bittersweet because she will miss working with her Marvel family, and getting to see them every 18 months to two years.
On July 7, 2021 analysts revealed that they expected the film to make approximately $140 million at the box office for the July 7th weekend.
On July 8, 2021, it was revealed that Eric Pearson, the Black Widow screenwriter wrote the first draft of the movie in just 11 days.

On July 9, 2021, it was revealed that Disney/Marvel’s Black Widow kicked off its previews at 5PM on Friday earning a huge $13.2 Million at the box office, easily the best preview night to date during the pandemic besting Universal’s F9 ($7.1M) and Paramount’s A Quiet Place Part II ($4.8M). Furthermore, it was revealed that the film has received an 81% Certified Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes. Lastly, it was also mentioned that the Black Widow film also opened in a further 30 material markets, including Germany, Russia, Australia, Japan, Korea, Brazil and Mexico, taking its full total to 41 material markets to date, with the first two days racking up an estimated $22.4M to date.

On July 9, 2021, Scarlett Johansson said in an interview that the film had many iterations, and that in one of them Yelena and Natasha were adversaries and Yelena tried to dethrone her, and then there was another version that was "really existential and kind of weird", but neither she nor Kevin Feige liked them and thought it wouldn't work.

On July 11, 2021, it was revealed that over the past weekend, the premiere of Marvel's Black Widow was the standout winner, raking in over $80 million from theater ticket sales alone. So far, its weekend debut has blown other hits like Godzilla vs Kong, Mortal Kombat, and even powerhouse action franchises like F9 out of the water.

On July 12, 2021, Olga Kurylenko confirmed that there is so much background story of Taskmaster, but there was no time to show it all. She also said that it's possible to return on future films, and she would like it. She also said that her mother didn't even know that she was in the movie, and she still haven't watch it.

On July 15, 2021, it was announced that the film will be released in India on Disney+ Hotstar, skipping theatrical run. The film was released on September 3, 2021, along with its Indian language dubs.

Rumors surfaced long ago about an Iron Man cameo in the movie, however Eric Pearson revealed that the only time he saw his name anywhere was in an old version of the script as a "flag-planted reminder" about the last scene of Natasha and Tony on Captain America: Civil War.
Originally, in the final scenes, Natasha Romanoff would be arrested by Secretary Ross and six agents would take her and put into the SUV. The scene was cut but one shot is visible on trailers.
Michelle Lee said that her character Oksana, had a whole backstory, but that she could only reflect it in her performance.

Black Widow marked the final performance of William Hurt before his death in March 2022 although The King's Daughter which was originally filmed in 2014 was released after this film. This was his final appearance as Ross in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
Blade marks the second character that Mahershala Ali had played following his portrayal of Cottonmouth in Luke Cage.
Blade has been pushed back twice, from November 3, 2023 to September 6, 2024 to February 14, 2025.
Flying Lotus was set to compose the score for Blade before being dropped from the project.

The film's costume designer Ruth E. Carter repurposed numerous designs and concepts intended for Blade, for the production of the action-horror film Sinners with director Ryan Coogler, whom she previously worked with on Black Panther and Black Panther: Wakanda Forever. Blade was originally intended to be a period piece film set in the 1920s at an earlier point in pre-production, and Sinners co-producer Sev Ohanian revealed in an interview with ScreenCrush that Marvel Studios allowed access to Carter's warehouse of "period-appropriate" clothing, and for the Sinners production crew to purchase the costumes "at price" when Blade indefinitely halted development due to the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strikes.
Blade is a reboot of the Blade trilogy.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The original title of Captain America: New World Order was the same title as the first episode of The Falcon and The Winter Soldier.

The film's storyline adapts some ellements of the 1974 "Secret Empire" story arc, where Captain America contends with the President of the United States and has to fight fellow Americans, and Donny Cates' Hulk storyline "Smashtronaut" where Thaddeus Ross becomes President and uses gamma technology for American interests. Interestingly, the film shares a subtitle with a miniseries tie-in to the 2017 version of "Secret Empire."
Characters from the movie adapted from the comics are Ruth Bat-Seraph, Leila Taylor, Seth Voelker/Sidewinder, Davis Lawfers/Copperhead and Dennis Dunphy.

The second official poster of Captain America: Brave New World, featuring Captain America protecting himself from Red Hulk's punch with his shield, is a direct homage to the cover of Captain America #230, featuring Steve Rogers and Hulk in the same positions.
Following William Hurt's passing, Thaddeus Ross was recast as Harrison Ford.
The film was originally titled Captain America: New World Order before it was renamed to Captain America: Brave New World.

The film marks the third time a Marvel Cinematic Universe franchise has gotten a fourth movie following The Avengers and Thor. However, it is the first franchise to get a series as well as four films.
Bucky Barnes is the only character who appeared in all Captain America films. The only characters who appeared in all three previous films are Steve Rogers, Bucky Barnes and the Watcher Informant.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On Steve Rogers' desk in the Avengers Compound, Rogers still has his drawing of himself as a monkey on a unicycle which he drew in Captain America: The First Avenger.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When the Avengers initially argue over the Sokovia Accords, Tony Stark mentions how when he found out his weapons were being misused, he shut down his weapon production division, referencing the event of Iron Man.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: In one scene when Tony Stark and Steve Rogers are talking, Tony mentions how he almost lost Pepper Potts a few years back. This happened in Iron Man 3.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Miriam Sharpe tells Tony Stark that her son died in Sokovia, referring to the Ultron Offensive that took place in Avengers: Age of Ultron.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: In the scene where Secretary Thaddeus Ross meets with the Avengers, he shows footage from the films The Avengers, Captain America: The Winter Soldier and Avengers: Age of Ultron. In the same scene, Ross asks Steve if he knows where Thor and Bruce Banner are.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When the trigger words have finished being spoken, Bucky Barnes replies with "Ready to comply." This is a reference to the Faustus Method established in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., where the question was asked "Are you ready to comply?"

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: During the Battle at the Hydra Siberian Facility, when Captain America is asked by Iron Man to stand down, he responds "I could do this all day". This is phrase is also said twice in Captain America: The First Avenger, when Steve Rogers is beaten by a bully in an alley and later when he was held prisoner by Red Skull.

While he was talking about F.R.I.D.A.Y., Tony Stark mentioned that he pictured her as a redhead (although he admitted that he was probably thinking of someone else). This is a reference her latest holographic appearances in the comics.

The working title that was used to create the film was "Sputnik". In the comics, "Sputnik" used to trigger the Winter Soldier's mind control, much like the sequence ""Longing, Rusted, Seventeen, Daybreak, Furnace, Nine, Benign, Homecoming, One, Freight Car" for his cinematic counterpart.
The Leipzig-Halle Airport airport is an allusion to Baron Zemo's original birthplace.

facts.section: References to Marvel Comics / Parallelisms with the Civil War comic book storyline
facts.text: In the comics, the Civil War storyline was centered around superheroes registering their secret identities and the details of their powers and abilities with the government, a plot point that would not work in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which has largely eschewed the secret identity trope. Kevin Feige has said that this storyline will focus on government regulation of the heroes after the battle in Avengers: Age of Ultron.

facts.section: References to Marvel Comics / Parallelisms with the Civil War comic book storyline
facts.text: In the movie, Wanda Maximoff accidentally killed a group of Wakandan volunteers in Lagos while she was trying to contain Crossbones's suicidal explosion, which was the last of the critical events that lead to the approval of the Sokovia Accords. In the comics, the supercriminal Nitro caused an explosion in Stamford, Connecticut, during his battle with the superhero Speedball, which killed hundreds of people including an elementary school, which lead to the approval of the Superhuman Registration Act.

facts.section: References to Marvel Comics / Parallelisms with the Civil War comic book storyline
facts.text: Peggy Carter's speech that her niece Sharon quoted during her eulogy is the same speech Captain America gave to Spider-Man in Amazing Spider-Man, during the Civil War storyline.

facts.section: References to Marvel Comics / Parallelisms with the Civil War comic book storyline
facts.text: In the film both Scott Lang becoming Giant-Man and War Machine getting badly injured are a nod towards the second Giant-Man in the comics Bill Foster who was an Anti-Registration hero in the Civil War who was killed by Thor's clone Ragnarok, who unlike Vision in the film did it on his own accord, rather than by accident.

facts.section: References to Marvel Comics / Parallelisms with the Civil War comic book storyline
facts.text: In the Civil War comics, Spider-Man was on the Pro-Registration side until he defected to the Anti-Registration side after learning how they were imprisoning the captured heroes in the Negative Zone without due process until they agreed to register. In the film, after Spider-Man is injured during the battle at the airport in Germany, Iron Man removes him from the team and sends him back home to New York.

facts.section: References to Marvel Comics / Parallelisms with the Civil War comic book storyline
facts.text: The Raft prison serves in this adaptation as the counterpart of Prison 42, with it being the place in which Tony Stark's Pro-Registration side imprisons members of the Anti-Registration. In a way, they also adapt the escape from the prison, though it is mostly left off screen, and to the tie-in comics for Infinity War.

During the Battle at Leipzig-Halle Airport, Spider-Man mentions the film Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back (and uses one move from the film against Ant-Man). The film and the Star Wars franchise, like Marvel Studios and the Marvel Cinematic Universe, are part of Disney.

facts.section: References to the Russo Brothers and their Other Works
facts.text: Co-director Joe Russo portrayed the psychiatrist Theo Broussard, who was killed and replaced by Helmut Zemo during the course of the movie.

facts.section: References to the Russo Brothers and their Other Works
facts.text: Ann Russo, Anthony Russo's wife, provided the voice of Heike Zemo in the message box of Helmut Zemo's phone.

facts.section: References to the Russo Brothers and their Other Works
facts.text: The "Bluth Company Stair Car" from Arrested Development can be seen in the battle at the Leipzig-Halle Airport. The Russo brothers directed many episodes of the TV series, including the pilot.

facts.section: References to the Russo Brothers and their Other Works
facts.text: Jim Rash, who worked with the Russo Brothers in Community, has a cameo in the movie as a Dean of the MIT.

facts.section: References to the Russo Brothers and their Other Works
facts.text: In the film, Helmut Zemo torture and kills Vasily Karpov in his refuge in Cleveland. Cleveland is the birth town of the Russo Brothers.

Marvel Studios initially announced Captain America: Civil War as Captain America: Serpent Society as a joke during the announcement of the film slate for Phase Three of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige stated: "We had this great idea because Civil War's first up, right? But we don't blow our wad on the presentation with Civil War right at the front of it. A guy named Mike Pasciullo had the idea to put Serpent Society on there, and I thought it was awesome and hilarious. A part of me thought, 'Are people going to love Serpent Society and think that'd be really cool? Now it's on the radar."
Despite not having been officially revealed by Marvel Studios, Robert Downey Jr. said Mark Ruffalo would be in the film; this did not prove true.
Tony Stark's de-aged appearance is based on Robert Downey Jr.'s appearance in the 1987 film Less Than Zero.
The Art of Captain America: Civil War features a concept art image of Bryan Cranston as Thaddeus Ross.
Scott Adkins was intended to have a role in the film, but his part was written out due to script changes. Adkins later played Lucian Aster in Doctor Strange.
Civil War is the first appearance of Captain America that doesn't feature him riding a motorcycle.
Sebastian Stan speaks his native tongue, Romanian language when his character Bucky Barnes is hiding in Romania.
This was released on the 75th anniversary of Captain America, the 50th anniversary of Black Panther, and the 10th anniversary of the Civil War comic the film was based on.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The film was originally meant to be a standalone film, but after Joss Whedon was hired to direct The Avengers (2012) he was given a copy of the film's script and made a few rewrites to tie it in to the Marvel Cinematic Universe: "I just got to make some character connections. The structure of the thing was really tight and I loved it, but there were a couple of opportunities to find his voice a little bit - and some of the other characters - and make the connections so that you understood exactly why he wanted to be who he wanted to be. And progressing through the script to flesh it out a little bit."

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: This is the first MCU film to be set mainly in the past of the present day, however, the opening is set in 2011, while the main events are set in the 1940s.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Hydra is introduced in the MCU. However, after the reveal that Hydra had infiltrated S.H.I.E.L.D. in Captain America: The Winter Soldier members of the sleeping agency made an appearance before the proper introduction of the organization. For example, Senator Stern appeared in Iron Man 2 while Jasper Sitwell was first seen in Thor.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When Johann Schmidt is searching for the Tesseract at the beginning of the film, he shoots the man hiding it and blood splatters on his Hydra pin. The blood only splatters on the skull part of his Hydra pin, foreshadowing his becoming the Red Skull.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Within the Norwegian church, there is a statue of a kneeling Norseman. A larger version of the statue is later seen in Thor's vision in Avengers: Age of Ultron. According to set photos, the large statue was set to return in Avengers: Infinity War.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Elements from the Nordic mythology are mentioned throughout the film. For example, the Asgardians from Thor are the "Gods" referenced by Schmidt. Yggdrasil is also mentioned.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Though not introduced by their name, the Infinity Stones make a proper appearance in the MCU through the Tesseract, later revealed to be the Space Stone. A blueprint of the Cube can be seen in Iron Man 2.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: In 1943, Steve Rogers mentions his deceased parents, Joseph and Sarah Rogers. Despite not being mentioned, in the comic prelude, Captain America: First Vengeance, it is revealed that Rogers used to hang out in Hell's Kitchen.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Rogers' phrase "I can do this all day" is later brought up in future MCU installments such as Captain America: Civil War and Avengers: Endgame.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The film marks the first chronological appearance of the Stark Expo which is labelled as World Exposition of Tomorrow. The Stark Expo made its first appearance in Iron Man 2.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When Bucky takes Steve to the World's Fair near the beginning of the film he says, "We're going to the future" - a foreshadowing that Steve Rogers will actually go to the future at the end of the film.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: During the Stark Expo presentation, Howard Stark presents the Hovercar, a car that uses gravitic reversion technology. The device is said to be a protoype. A better design of the Hovercar is seen in the TV series Agent Carter during the episode Hollywood Ending. In Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., Coulson's car L.O.L.A. also uses this technology.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The Strategic Scientific Reserve is introduced in the MCU being the predecessor of S.H.I.E.L.D. which played a big role in Marvel Studios' Phase One.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When Abraham Erskine tells Rogers the history of Hydra and Schmidt, he mentions that Schmidt based his scientific investigations on known myths in the world such as Asgard and other ancient creatures. This part of Hydra's history is further expanded in the third season of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When chasing down the Hydra agent after being injected with the super soldier serum, Steve picks up a Taxi Cab door. The cab company is 'Lucky Star Cab Company' - with the name circling the star for a logo - resembling and foreshadowing the iconic shield that Steve eventually wields as Captain America.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Even though the vial of serum stolen by the Hydra agent is broken, another showed up in The Incredible Hulk to be injected into Emil Blonsky (making him the Abomination). You can even see "Vita-Rays" written on the refrigerated storage container. According to canon many attempts were made to replicate the Super-Soldier experiment, but for a yet-unexplained reason it only ever worked on Steve Rogers. This was also brought up in other MCU TV series such as Agent Carter where it was mentioned that the government took 12 samples of Rogers' blood and by 1946 they had wasted most of it with no success.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The first Captain America comic makes a cameo in the film. In real life the movie is inspired by the comic book, while in the movie the comic book is inspired by "real life".

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Laura Haddock portrays an unnamed Captain America fan. The actress would later play Meredith Quill in Guardians of the Galaxy and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2. When questioned by this by a fan, James Gunn replied that Haddock was portraying Peter Quill's Grandmother, thus Meredith's mother. However, he was joking.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The Howling Commandos are introduced in the MCU.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When Captain America attacks the base and finds the prisoners, he finds Barnes strapped to a table. It was later revealed in Captain America: The Winter Soldier that Arnim Zola had experimented on him. This would help Barnes to survive to his fall during the Capture of Arnim Zola. This had set up Barnes' future appearance as the Winter Soldier, storyline that came to life in the sequel of the film.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The Red Skull is only referred to as the "Red Skull" once in the movie, by the German SS officer sent by Hitler. However, in future MCU productions such as Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Captain America: The Winter Soldier, Schmidt is mentioned as "Red Skull" rather than Schmidt.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: When Steve discovers the gunmetal circular shield in the development office of Howard Stark, he asks what it's made from. Vibranium is a fictional element in the Marvel universe that comes from the country of Wakanda, the land where Black Panther, another Marvel superhero, lives. Wakanda had been teased in Iron Man 2 and later mentioned in Avengers: Age of Ultron before making a proper appearance in Captain America: Civil War and Black Panther. The country would also be mentioned in the MCU TV show Runaways.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Just before his apparent death, Bucky Barnes wields Captain America's shield. In the comics, when Steve Rogers was killed, Bucky took over as Captain America.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Howard Stark finds the lost Tesseract at the end, which leads him to creating blue print designs about the cubes structure and overall power, which can be seen in a case of paperwork that Tony Stark looks through in the middle of Iron Man 2.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Nick Fury has an appearance by the end of the film in the present day telling Rogers that he had been gone for nearly 70 years.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: A post-credits caption promises ''Captain America will return in The Avengers''.

Arnim Zola's first appearance, in the form of his face as an image on a television screen, is evocative of the "classic" comic-book Zola, whose body was a headless hulk with a viewscreen on its chest displaying an image of his face.

The special forces unit that Captain America assembles and leads is an amalgamation of the characters of Marvel Comics' World War II period titles. These are the 1960s war title, "Sgt. Fury and his Howling Commandos" about an elite special forces infantry unit and the 1970s "The Invaders," about a superhero team operating during the war under the command of Captain America. The contributions of the former title include most of the soldier characters, while the latter includes Captain America, Bucky and James Montgomery Falsworth, who appears in the comic book as the British superhero, Union Jack.

In the exhibition, there is a mannequin in a red jumpsuit under a glass dome. That is a reference to the android, the original Human Torch, the first superhero created by Timely Comics (October 1939), which eventually became Marvel Comics. He was also part of The Invaders along with Namor and Captain America. Marvel Comics recycled the name and abilities with the Fantastic Four's Johnny Storm (1961).
The Captain America comic book shown in the movies bears the cover of the actual Captain America #1 released in 1941.

During the escape from the Hydra facility, Dugan and Jones steal a tank. As they drive away, you hear Dugan exclaim "Wahoo!" In the comics, this is the battle cry of the Howling Commandos, of which both men are members.

In the final scene of the film, Captain America attempts to break out of the S.H.I.E.L.D. facility he is at, thinking he was captured by the enemy before learning about the modern world. This is based on his Ultimate Marvel counterpart who did the same thing in Ultimates #3.

Stan Lee's cameo appearance in this film is an exception in the tradition of him appearing in films featuring Marvel Comics superheroes. In this case, Lee had nothing to do with the initial creation of Captain America, but his first story he ever wrote was "Captain America Foils the Traitor's Revenge" in Captain America Comics #3 in 1941, which also had the first appearance of Captain America throwing his shield as a weapon. In addition, he, along with Jack Kirby, was responsible for successfully reviving the character in 1964 in The Avengers #4 and reestablishing him as a major figure in the Marvel Universe.

Originally cameo appearances were planned in the film for Wolverine and Magneto, who were present during World War II (Logan was a soldier and Lensherr was a prisoner of war). However, these cameos were scrapped due to rights issues. Before the rights to the "X-Men" franchise reverted to Marvel on December 14th 2017, they belonged to 20th Century Fox.
Originally cameo appearances were planned in the film for Namor, the Prince of Atlantis, but this was scrapped.

This is the fifth live-action adaptation for Captain America. The first was the serial, Captain America (1944); the second was the TV movie Captain America (1979) and its sequel, Captain America II: Death Too Soon (1979), and the fourth was the theatrical film Captain America (1990).

In the 1979 made for TV movies, Steve Rogers makes his living as an artist. As a homage, in this newer version, Steve Rogers sketches costumes designs for Howard Stark and is caught doodling pictures of himself as a circus monkey.

The Red Skull searches for a powerful cube-shaped artifact, the Tesseract. In Transformers, Hugo Weaving voiced the villain Megatron, who also searched for a similar cosmic cube-shaped relic (the All-Spark).
The scene where Chester Phillips flipped a switch to accelerate a car is an homage to a similar scene in Men in Black, where Tommy Lee Jones' character does the same.
The sniper rifle Bucky uses to save Cap is a modified 1941 Johnson rifle, which was adopted in limited numbers by the US Marine Corps.
Hydra's futurist aircraft take their designs from actual WWII German concepts such as the Horten H.XVIII flying wing bomber and Triebflügeljäger fighter plane.
WILHELM SCREAM: Rogers is pursued by Hydra soldiers on motorcycles, but releases a flamethrower defense. One screams as he swerves, loses control and is thrown headlong.

During the Attack on Hydra Headquarters, Captain America pulls the pin out of a Model 24 grenade strapped to the side of a Hydra motorcycle, causing an explosion which kills the driver. In reality, Model 24 grenades did not have a pin, but rather, a pull cord.

The final shortlist for the lead role consisted of Garrett Hedlund, Channing Tatum, Scott Porter, Mike Vogel, Ryan Phillippe, Sebastian Stan, Chris Evans, Wilson Bethel, John Krasinski, Michael Cassidy, Chace Crawford, and Jensen Ackles. Both Kellan Lutz and Alexander Skarsgård auditioned for the lead role, while Sam Worthington and Will Smith were in early talks. The role went to Chris Evans, who has already played another Marvel superhero, Johnny Storm/Human Torch in Fantastic Four (2005) and Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007). Tatum was signed on to play Remy LeBeau/Gambit in a solo Gambit movie which was postponed and later shelved for 20th Century Studios. Tatum made a cameo as Remy LeBeau/Gambit in Deadpool & Wolverine. Bethel later portrayed Benjamin Poindexter in Daredevil. Krasinski made a much a anticipated cameo as Reed Richards/Mister Fantastic in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness as he was a popular choice to play the role. Smith later played Deadshot in the DC Extended Universe production Suicide Squad.
Emily Blunt turned down the role of Peggy Carter. Other actresses considered for the role were Alice Eve and Keira Knightley. Eve later played Mary Walker in Iron Fist.
Sebastian Stan was considered for the role of Captain America, but got the role of Bucky Barnes instead.

Jon Favreau was originally chosen by Marvel Studios to direct this film, but he chose to direct Iron Man (2008). Nick Cassavetes, was also considered to direct this film, and had been set as a director for Iron Man (2008) in December 2004.
Despite being "The First Avenger", it is the last solo Avenger film to be released before the team-up film, The Avengers (2012).

According to producer Avi Arad: "The biggest opportunity with Captain America is as a man 'out of time', coming back today, looking at our world through the eyes of someone who thought the perfect world was small-town America. Sixty years go by, and who are we today? Are we better?"
Joe Johnston was chosen as the film's director for his work on the period adventure films The Rocketeer (1991), October Sky (1999) and Hidalgo (2004).

Louis Leterrier viewed some of the concept art for the film, and was impressed enough to offer his services, but Marvel Studios turned him down. However, his film The Incredible Hulk (2008) provides a small appearance by Captain America: a deleted scene set in the Arctic.
Screenwriter David Self, who wrote a draft of the script, claimed Captain America was his favorite childhood superhero: "My dad told me I could one day be Captain America."

Chris Evans was attracted to the role of Captain America by its character: "Even if it wasn't a comic book. I think the story of Steve Rogers is great. He's a great guy. Even if it was just a script about anybody, I would probably want to do it. It wasn't necessarily about the comic itself. He's a great character to play; he just happens to be a comic book character."
Chris Evans declined the role three times before accepting the part. After that, he had a meeting with the director and the producers who convinced him to take the role.
To prepare for his role as Bucky, Sebastian Stan watched many World War II films/documentaries, and drew inspiration from Band of Brothers (2001).
Stanley Tucci took the role of Dr. Abraham Erskine because the role enabled him to use a German accent, which he always wanted to do.
To prepare for her role as Peggy Carter, Hayley Atwell trained six days a week.
Joe Simon, who created the "Captain America" comic in 1941 (before Stan Lee revived it in 1964), was approached to make a cameo appearance in the film.
Hugo Weaving based the Red Skull's accent on renowned German filmmakers Werner Herzog and Klaus Maria Brandauer.
The film was originally going to be film in Manhattan Beach, California but moved it to London, England due of the tax breaks to films costing over $75 million.
Captain America was put on hold during the 2007–2008 Writers Guild of America strike.

Tommy Lee Jones who plays Colonel Chester Phillips in this film, also appeared as Two-Face/Harvey Dent in Batman Forever (1995). Both Captain America and Batman faced off in the Marvel vs. DC crossover in 1996.
Hayley Atwell based her performance as Peggy Carter on Ginger Rogers: "She can do everything Captain America can do, but backwards and in high heels."
The final Paramount Pictures film produced with Marvel Studios. Disney bought the rights to The Avengers (2012) and Iron Man 3 (2013).

Contrary to popular belief, a body double was not used for Chris Evans for the scenes when he was skinny. The filmmakers had originally planned to hire a body double and superimpose Evans' face onto the double's body, but ultimately scrapped the idea since director Joe Johnston claimed that Evans moved in a unique way and that no body double could replicate his movements. Ultimately, the filmmakers utilized digital technology to "shrink" Evans down, essentially erasing portions of his physique, until they came up with what the filmmakers called "Skinny Steve". Over 250 shots were filmed like this, and because the shrinking process left empty space in the background, many of the scenes had to filmed in front of a green screen so that they could superimpose the backgrounds back into the scene.
