Tom Hiddleston spoke of his role as Loki in an interview by saying, "I can tell you that it's all of them against me. I am the super villain. So it's Iron Man, the Incredible Hulk, Captain America, Thor, Hawkeye, Black Widow and Nick Fury forming a team because I've got so bad ass."

Tom Hiddleston describes Loki in this film as having evolved since Thor: "How pleasant an experience is it to disappear into a wormhole that was created by some super-nuclear explosion of his own making? I think by the time Loki shows up he's seen a few things and has bigger things in mind than just his brother and Asgard..."

According to Director Joss Whedon, the original cut of the movie was over 3 hours long. There will be about 30 minutes of the excised footage included in the DVD Release, most of which revolves around Steve Rogers (Captain America). Whedon revealed that one of these scenes involved Rogers struggling to adjust to the modern world in his Brooklyn apartment and another revealed Steve Rogers' reunion with Peggy Carter, his love interest from Captain America: The First Avenger.
Tom Hiddleston revealed in an interview with the Guardian that the code name for the film early in its production was 'Group Hug'.

The film has an unusually high number of Academy Award nominees in the cast for any movie which includes the following: Robert Downey Jr.; Samuel L. Jackson; Jeremy Renner; and Mark Ruffalo. However, it still falls short of the five in Iron Man 2: Downey Jr.; Jackson; Gwyneth Paltrow; Mickey Rourke; and Don Cheadle.
This is the second time that Bruce Banner/Hulk and Thor have appeared together in a movie. They previously appeared together in The Incredible Hulk Returns.
This movie marks the third time Samuel L. Jackson and Scarlett Johansson have appeared in the same film. The previous two were Avengers prequel Iron Man 2 and The Spirit.
Both Chris Evans and Scarlett Johansson have work together in The Perfect Score and The Nanny Diaries.

With Samuel L. Jackson's role as Nick Fury in this film, he is now the third actor after Christopher Reeve (in the DC Comics-based Superman films) and Hugh Jackman (who has appeared in all X-Men movies) to play the same comic book superhero in five different movies.
Every time Tony Stark ate something in the movie (With the exception of the post-credits scene) was not scripted, Robert Downey Jr. was just hungry.
During the post-credits scene, Chris Evans, who portrayed Captain America, constantly covers his face because he was growing a beard for the film Snowpiercer when that scene was filmed.
It has been reported that after the showing of the post-credits scene, shawarma sales increased incredibly.
When Thor fires lightning at Iron Man, J.A.R.V.I.S. says that the armor's power-level is at 400%, while the HUD shows that it is actually at 475%.

Betty Ross, Bruce Banner's love interest, is the only pre-Avengers love interest not to appear in The Avengers in any capacity. Gwyneth Paltrow reprised her role as Pepper Potts, Tony Stark's love interest. Jane Foster, Thor's love interest, was mentioned by Phil Coulson to have been relocated by S.H.I.E.L.D. after Loki captured Erik Selvig. And during his workout, Steve Rogers remembered his love interest during World War II, Peggy Carter.

This was the third highest-grossing film of all time at the time of its release (behind Avatar and Titanic) and the highest-grossing film distributed by Disney, surpassing Toy Story 3, until it was surpassed by Star Wars: The Force Awakens in 2015. It is, as of 2026, the thirteenth highest-grossing film of all time, and the eighth highest-grossing film distributed by Disney.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The Duel of Harlem from The Incredible Hulk and the Battle of New York from The Avengers are both seen on newspapers.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Luke Cage, Iron Fist, Daredevil, and Jessica Jones all star in the series, reprising their roles from Luke Cage, Iron Fist, Daredevil, and Jessica Jones respectively. Additionally, various characters from The Defenders Saga appear, including Malcolm Ducasse, Foggy Nelson, Colleen Wing, Misty Knight, Bakuto, Trish Walker, Karen Page, Elektra, Claire Temple, Stick, Madame Gao, and Jeri Hogarth.

One of the trailers shows black and white security camera footage of the four Defenders in an elevator with a time stamp in the top right corner. When Jessica Jones disables the camera, the time code says 8:18:20:17 in hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds. This is a reference to the release date of the show on August 18th, 2017.

works.work: The Falcon and The Winter Soldier

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On September 11, 2020, Sebastian Stan, in regards to what it felt like shooting the Disney+ series went onto say how, "It felt like both. In a lot of ways, it felt like a movie. What I loved about it was that, tonally, it was very much in the same world that Captain America: The Winter Soldier was, which was one of my favorite experiences that I’ve ever had, period," Stan explained. "So, in a sense, it was grounded and very much in the world as we know it. But, it’s also really jam-packed with a lot of massive, massive action scenes mixed with deep focus on character. These characters are getting so much more mileage for all of us to explore them. We can put them in situations that we’ve never been able to put them in before because you now have six hours as opposed to two."

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On December 12, 2020, at the Investor's Day event a trailer that is just under two minutes of footage was released, where viewers have learned a couple tonal themes of the series, particularly revolving around Anthony Mackie's growth from supporting character to lead hero. The opening shots of the trailer reveal a Captain America Museum of sorts, with numerous 1940s newspaper headlines commanding screens. Some of those headlines directly reference events from Captain America: The First Avenger; '400 PRISONERS LIBERATED' calls back to Steve Rogers's first Captain America mission, when he goes against his general's orders and saves Bucky, the Howling Commandos, and hundreds more from a Hydra facility; Below that particular headline is a poster that reads 'TOUR CANCELED,' which is referencing the end of Cap's song-and-dance routine after he becomes a full-fledged member of the United States Army; 'NAZIS IN NEW YORK: MYSTERY MAN SAVES CHILD' is from when Cap chases down the Hydra agent that blew up the Super Soldier lab in his first experience in his new bulky body; In the next shots of the trailer, numerous black and white images of Steve Rogers are shown. From left to right, a pre-Super Soldier serum Steve from when he was training at Camp Lehigh and Captain America using a car door as a shield during that initial Nazi chase; Finally, Cap can be viewed giving orders during that World War II montage.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On January 01, 2021, Georges St-Pierre expressed his excitement to be back in the MCU while talking to Inspired Traveler. As it has already been revealed, he is set to return as Georges Batroc, who hasn't been seen since his debut in 2014's Captain America: The Winter Soldier, he acknowledged the "huge budget" that The Falcon and The Winter Soldier was granted and admitted the show is "the biggest thing" he's ever done. He went onto further state that, "It's a huge budget. It's the biggest thing I've done in my life. It’s really big. I've been taking classes to become an actor for a while now. I am working very hard on this. I am very proud of the job I have done on the show. I can’t wait for people to see the result of my work."; St-Pierre explained that he's "a bit of a nerd" for the Marvel Cinematic Universe, even saying that his passion for mixed martial arts can be credited in part to "this passion" that he now gets to explore further in the MCU; He finished his interview by saying that, "I’m a bit of a nerd in this universe. I think this passion influenced me in my adventure with mixed martial arts. When I was in the cage I was like a superhero and as soon as I stepped out of the arena I was back to being a normal human being."

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: While on The Jess Cagle Show, Mackie when asked if Falcon would become Captain America, Mackie shared that, "we don't know that yet. The show, the idea of the show is basically, you know, and at the end of Avengers: Endgame, Cap decided he was going into retirement and he asked me if I would take up the shield, but at no point in time did I agree to or say that I would be Captain America," and went on to enigmatically remark, "So, the show walks the line of who is going to take up the shield and who's going to be Captain America if Steve isn't coming back."

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On January 15, 2021, a Hasbro action figure of Sam Wilson dressed in a Captain America costume was leaked. The name badge on the toy's packaging reads Captain America rather than Wilson's more familiar superhero title, The Falcon. In addition, the packaging features an image of actor Anthony Mackie as Wilson dressed in the Captain America costume.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On March 15, 2021, Mackie revealed in a recent interview with The Toronto Sun that he "requested" a love story with Black Widow. Also on this day, the release of The Falcon and The Winter Soldier with only a few short days away, a major part of its marketing campaign included a series of promos released in partnership with Xbox that show Anthony Mackie's Falcon playing various games on the Xbox Series X console. These promos have included several Easter eggs to the MCU already and offered fans the best look yet at Sam Wilson's new wings. In one of the commercials, the identity of NoobMaster69 was revealed.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On March 18, 2021, as part of the virtual launch event for Marvel's The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, Elizabeth Olsen and Paul Bettany were on hand to congratulate the cast of the show and voice their excitement for seeing Sam Wilson and Bucky Barnes lead their own show.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On March 19, 2021, a scene in the first episode of The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, the audience was treated to a scene where Don Cheadle's War Machine and Anthony Mackie's Sam Wilson walk through a Captain America memorial exhibit as they discuss the mantle that Steve left behind. On one part of the exhibit, there is a quote explaining what exactly happened to Chris Evans' Steve Rogers following the events of Avengers: Endgame that says: With the death of Iron Man, Steve Rogers honored his friend by finally retiring and laying down his shield, enjoying the world he had fought so hard to protect. With this exhibit we honor the life and legacy of Steve Rogers, Captain America: patriot, soldier, hero.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On March 30th, 2021, Wyatt Russell revealed on Jimmy Kimmel Live! that for his role on The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, he asked for one of the original Cap costumes. But instead they gave him a new suit instead.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On April 4, 2021, Wyatt Russell revealed in an interview that he doesn't know if his character has a future in the MCU beyond his appearances throughout The Falcon and The Winter Soldier.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: In a pivotal moment between Ayo and Bucky in Episode 4: The Whole World Is Watching, the Dora Milaje arrive in Latvia after learning that Baron Zemo, who murdered Wakanda's King T'Chaka in Captain America: Civil War, has been freed from prison. The Dora Milaje's demand that Zemo be handed over leads to a skirmish, during which Ayo quickly ends her fight with Bucky by using a failsafe to deactivate and detach his metal arm.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On April 16, 2021, Julia Louis-Dreyfus made her surprise MCU debut as Contessa Valentina Allegra de Fontaine in Truth, the penultimate episode of The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, but according to sources close to the production, Louis-Dreyfus was slated to first appear in the Black Widow film which, in a pre-COVID world, was scheduled to debut in theaters May 1, 2020. But Marvel, reportedly, now has even bigger ambitions for Louis-Dreyfus's villainous figure.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: In Truth, the fifth episode of The Falcon and The Winter Soldier Bucky Barnes handed Baron Helmut Zemo over to the Dora Milaje of Wakanda. As he's being taken away, Ayo explicitly states that Zemo will be put in the Raft, which was seen in Captain America: Civil War, where Avengers that supported Captain America were imprisoned alongside dangerous criminals.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On April 16, 2021, in Truth, the fifth episode of The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, Sharon Carter is seen on a phone call in Madripoor with an unknown personality. When turning on the subtitles during this scene, it's revealed that Sharon is speaking to Georges St-Pierre's Georges Batroc as she lets him know about the undisclosed job. While his actual dialogue isn't revealed, the subtitles for his end of the call say "Batroc speaking French."

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On April 19, 2021, it was revealed that The Falcon and the Winter Solider will be submitted as a Drama Series at this year's Emmy Awards, marking a shift from its expected placement in the Limited Series categories. This way, it avoids direct competition with WandaVision, which has been submitted for the Limited Series category instead.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On April 20, 2021, it was once again reported that it's looking more and more possible that Marvel's The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, as well as the upcoming Loki series, could see multiple seasons, but WandaVision instead looks more likely than ever to be a one-and-done show.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On April 22, 2021, Marvel Studios posted a binge guide leading up to The Falcon and The Winter Soldier finale on Friday April 23, 2021, and they additionally promised 'surprises throughout the day.'.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On April 23,2021, shortly after The Falcon and The Winter Soldier aired its 6th episode, it was announced that Captain America 4 was greenlit with head writer Malcolm Spellman returning and co-writing the script with FAWS scribe Dalan Musson. No further details, including who exactly will wield the star-spangled shield, however no additional details were made available.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: On April 26, 2021, to celebrate Sam as the new Captain America, Marvel Studios has officially changed the banners on its Captain America social media pages on Twitter and Facebook from Chris Evans' Captain America to Anthony Mackie's.

On October 25, 2020, it was mentioned that in the series Helmut Zemo will also be getting his comic book accurate title of Baron Zemo. This was revealed via a Funko Pop of the character recently released as promotion for the series, and is now sporting the aforementioned title.

On February 11, 2021, the latest trailer that debuted during Super Bowl LV has revealed a first look at the Principality of Madripoor, which in Marvel Comics canon is located somewhere in Southeast Asia between Singapore and Sumatra, and over the years has played a major part in countless stories revolving around the X-Men. Traditionally, it is split into the affluent Hightown and the working class Lowtown, The Falcon and the Winter Soldier footage shows both sides of the island, from the sprawling cityscape where skyscrapers dominate the skyline to the dense urban areas.

On March 19, 2021, in one of his newsletters, former Captain America writer and Winter Soldier co-creator Ed Brubaker expressed his "mixed" feelings about the brand new Disney+ show The Falcon and The Winter Soldier. He expressed how he is really happy for Sebastian Stan, who he thinks is both a great guy, and the perfect Bucky/Winter Soldier. Along with being glad to see him get more screen time than in the past. He even admitted that while everyone at Marvel Studios that he has ever met (all the way up to Kevin Feige) have been nothing but kind to home. At the same time, for the most part all Steve Epting and him have gotten for creating the Winter Soldier and his storyline is a “thanks” here or there, and over the years that's become harder and harder to live with. Brubaker continued to elaborate, discussing how he loved his time at Marvel and how the lack of recognition and credit they've received for their creation ate away at him.
On April 11, 2021, Emily VanCamp revealed that she is very interested in wearing Sharon Carter's iconic white suit from the comics.

On April 19, 2021, it was revealed that since Friday April 16, 2021, when Julia Louis-Dreyfus' character of Contessa Valentina Allegra de Fontaine appeared in Truth, the series 5th episode, eBay sales of the character's first appearance in the comics have surged. It was further reported that at least 10 copies of Strange Tales #159, written by Jim Steranko and Roy Thomas and drawn by Marie Severin and Steranko, were sold by various vendors on Friday alone with elevated price points ranging from $1,000 - $4,000. This is compared to a copy with a 9.0 CGC sold days earlier on April 12 for $259.99, and one sold on April 7 with a 9.6 CGC for $565.

On April 26, 2021, Marvel Studios officially released a new poster for The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, showcasing Sam Wilson as the MCU's new Captain America. Alongside the release, a new Twitter Emoji showing Sam Wilson's Star-Spangled hero was also unveiled. His suit pays homage to the one Sam wore in the comics during his tenure as Captain America.

On October 7, 2020, it was revealed that Disney and McDonald's have teamed up to offer a new collection of Marvel Studio toys as part of the McDonald Happy Meals. The line up will feature the likes of Falcon, Winter Soldier, Wanda Maximoff, Vision, Groot, Hulkbuster, Wasp, Hulk and the Black Widow herself. This merchandise of toys is also tied to promotion for WandaVision and The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, two Disney+ shows expected to premiere in late 2020 and sometime in 2021 respectively.
The Falcon and The Winter Soldier was shooting in Prague, which is where the show was in production when things were shut down early in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

On October 18, 2020, it was also revealed that in addition to Danny Ramirez being confirmed as part of the cast in a pivotal role, the series is also in the process of finishing the last bit of production that was halted earlier this year due to the coronavirus pandemic.

On October 20, 2020, it was confirmed that despite this series being pushed to 2021, Fans of Captain America can now bring home his iconic shield thanks to Marvel Legends' new prop replica shield from The Falcon and the Winter Soldier. Marvel Legends' new Captain America life-sized shield prop replica is inspired by the shield that will be seen in the upcoming Disney+ series and measures 24"in across.

On October 21, 2020, Derek Kolstad teased that in regards to what's in store for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, some familiar faces from long ago in the MCU will make appearances on the show. He went onto further teased that they are layering some of these earliest Marvel Movies characters in and reinventing them in a way that's gonna shift the storytelling structure; While it's already known that Daniel Brühl’s Helmut Zemo is returning, it's also mentioned that The Winter Soldier’s Georges Batroc is making a return as well.
On November 4,2020, a newly revealed toy prototype provided the first glimpse of the design for Sam Wilson's Captain America costume in the series.

On November 8, 2020, Disney began to promote their Disney+ Marvel Cinematic Universe series in Latin America for its upcoming launch in the aforementioned region, releasing a video teasing several shows like The Falcon and The Winter Soldier and WandaVision.

On November 18, 2020, some official Marvel merchandise released in a Tokyo-based Marvel Pop Up store, shows a sticker featuring Sharon Carter wearing a hoodie on top of the word "Wanted," while a notebook highlights the character's full disguise. Other pieces of tie-in merchandise showcase the new costumes of Anthony Mackie's Sam Wilson and Sebastian Stan's Bucky Barnes; It appears that the former S.H.I.E.L.D. agent is still on the run from the government, potentially hinting that the Sokovia Accords are somehow still in effect after Avengers: Endgame.

On December 23, 2020, a new promotional a new image revealing the two title heroes in full costume began to circulate. Also on this day, it was revealed through a release on Weibo, Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige announced that a Marvel-themed musical that will premiere on Bilibili (a Chinese video-sharing website) on December 31,2020 to celebrate the new year and what the MCU has in store for Phase 4.

On January 11, 2021, Kevin Feige was asked what the audience can expect regarding the runtime of their MCU series, with Feige responding that "Well, we're looking a little differently. We're looking at it as developing them as either six hour-episodes, or nine or 10 half-hour episodes." He gave examples, such as WandaVision and The Falcon and The Winter Soldier having their runtimes "blurred" due to the nature of streaming. Feige then went onto say how, "for instance, WandaVision started that way and Falcon and the Winter Soldier as 30 minutes, but because it's streaming, it's Disney+, and the rules have blurred over the years, yes. Some can be 23 minutes. Some can be much longer than that." As a result, it was officially confirmed that in the case of The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, it was being developed as six 40-50-minute episodes.

On January 18, 2021, Kevin Feige would go on to acknowledge the unexpected similarities between The Blip and the COVID-19 pandemic, before reiterating that he wants any future references to Thanos' attack to "have more meaning behind it." As a result, Phase Four, will instead be focused on setting up new stories rather than looking back to past events.

On January 28, 2021, the series composer Henry Jackman hinted at the "less comfortable things" that The Falcon and the Winter Soldier will address by stating how with "having six hourly episodes, that’s more real estate than one of [the films]," said Jackman. "There's a bit more opportunity to go into psychological drama and explore backstories. And in this particular series, there’s very much serious issues, now more than ever, about what it means to hold [Cap's] shield and what kind of a person should ultimately be holding that shield, and with the history of this country, and how African Americans would feel about being Captain America or not. It’s still entertaining, but it touches on less comfortable things that give rise to some really impressive performances. It’s a great balance of entertainment and writing [centering] around more weighty issues."

On this same day Mackie admitted that he had his reservations about taking part in this Disney+ series, stating how "at the end of Avengers: Endgame, Sam didn’t accept the shield," Anthony Mackie said on The Rich Eisen Show. "If you remember, he told Steve, 'It doesn’t feel right because this shield is yours.' So, you know, the show is a long way of figuring around who's gonna be Captain America. Where the shield's gonna end up and if Captain America, if that moniker is gonna come back and somebody's gonna hold that moniker again." His fear was that it would be more campy than classy, stating that he "basically, thought this show was gonna be like the old school Batman, I thought it was gonna be some shitty… or some of the other shows where it’s like soap operas."; But in the end Mackie said he was surprised by "the quality of our show with the acting, with the scripts, with the development of the characters and everything was so high-level, so high-brow. I didn’t think there was any way Marvel would be able to carry that on to television."
On February 1, 2021, ahead of the March premiere of The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, a first look at the new costumes for two key characters, Baron Zemo and John Walker were released.
On February 7, 2021, the only trailer from Marvel Studios that was released during Super Bowl LV.
On February 9, 2021, it was revealed that the trailer for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier in 24 hours had received views that bested that of Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker.

On February 11, 2021, Anthony Mackie revealed that he had to learn how to throw Captain America's Shield, and admitted that he didn't realize how heavy it really was. He compared the shield to a 10-pound weight hanging off one's arm, which is not the easiest thing to deal with." In the same interview Sebastian Stan added that in these six episodes, viewers will see Sam and Bucky in a part action-packed superhero epic, part awkward buddy-comedy. Stan went on to joke that there's an odd-couple kind of back-and-forth there.

On February 13, 2021, it was revealed that in the United States, the show will receive a PG-13 rating. However, overseas (particularly in the Netherlands), it has been given a 16+, which is roughly the equivalent to a TV-MA or R-rating in the United States. Which in turns likely means it could also be given a 15 rating in the United Kingdom. All likely coming off the presumed levels of violence to be shown in the series. However, by February 18, 2021, it was confirmed that the series had received a TV-14 rating for "language and violence."
However, on February 18, 2021, it was mentioned that contrary to popular belief, the series is actually rated TV-14.

On February 16, 2021, it was announced that Legends will release new installments that will center around Anthony Mackie's Falcon, Sebastian Stan's Winter Soldier, Daniel Brühl's Helmut Zemo, and Emily VanCamp's Sharon Carter and will be coming in March 2021 to Disney+. Presumably a week before the premiere of The Falcon and The Winter Soldier. Also on this day, through an Instagram story on his Instagram account, Sebastian Stan agreed that Falcon, Wanda Maximoff and his character of the Winter Soldier definitely need some therapy due to all the trauma they have gone through in their appearances across several MCU films. Which further solidifies how mental Health is a central theme that is part of the two shows' DNA.

Emily VanCamp also recently told E! Online that the show will be a little more action-heavy and less weird than WandaVision. She did teased that there will be some elements of mystery, along with some good old-fashioned action that she promises people will love from those movies.

On February 17, 2021, Malcolm Spellman, the series showrunner admitted that he believes that The Falcon and The Winter Soldier is a nice progression with the mantle that the Black Panther film directed by Ryan Coogler and the legacy left behind by Chadwick Boseman. He went onto further say that is important to have these giant Black icons, which are not only necessary for Black kids, but also for white kids to start to absorb how black people can be big and heroic.

On February 20, 2021, Mackie went onto say that when they were shooting The Falcon and the Winter Soldier in Prague, that it was as big of a production a Marvel Disney+ can ultimately get, with the production value being estimated at costing hundreds of millions of dollars. However, he admitted that at the same time, there's a certain disconnect because there's so many people there. Typically, there's at least 250 people a day on-set that according Mackie you form these little pods, these little communities... Thus working for Marvel it's tight-knit.

On February 24, 2021, at Kevin Feige at his first TCA said that the reason for settling on only six episodes is because of budget. Feige went onto further state after a lot of discussion, telling the story of Sam and Bucky in six hours was what he and the other people at Marvel Studios ultimately landed on as the best way to tell our story. he added. In addition, he mentioned that shows aren't inexpensive, so the per-episode cost is very high.

On February 25, 2021, the official Twitter account for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier shared a TV spot that featured Baron Zemo in his full costume, adding in subtitles that confirm the character's identity now in the aforementioned Disney+ Marvel series.
On February 28, 2021, now that the first embargo has been lifted, critics have been able to start talking about the series, and many went onto praise the action in particular.

On March 1, 2021, while plot specifics have been kept under wraps for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, Anthony Mackie teased that the wings have become much more pliable and much more dynamic. He further added that Falcon Wings are much more of a winged force. In addition, Sebastian Stan noted how the addition of Walker on the show "very much makes sense in the series," while also teasing "another side to that character that people haven't seen or expected."; Since Mackie and Stan have taken up lead roles in the MCU for the first time, the actors went onto reveal that they were given earlier access to the series' scripts, which Mackie noted as being quite the refreshing experience.

On March 2, 2021, Sebastian Stan teased Bucky's mental state in The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, calling him a bit of a mess. He further added that in the series, viewers will find Bucky in a strange place, having just gotten out of an epic battle and left to deal with his own demons. Moreover, with the release of The Falcon and The Winter Soldier edging closer, the marketing for the series has begun to ramp up in a big way. As a result, billboards for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier have begun appearing in Los Angeles in recent days; with one of the posters spotted on an LA billboard revealing new art from the upcoming series. This being Sam seen with his iconic Falcon wings spread beside Bucky in front of a city with helicopters in its skyline.
On March 3, 2021, Mackie gave an interview in which he got candid about feeling the pressure to make sure that The Falcon and the Winter Soldier is not Marvel's first fail.
On March 5, 2021, Disney+ officially released two new episodes for Marvel Studios: Legends, featuring the summary of the heroic journey of Sam Wilson and Bucky Barnes from the Infinity Saga.

On March 8, 2021, Marvel Studios unveiled four new character posters for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, which feature Anthony Mackie as Sam Wilson aka The Falcon, Sebastian Stan as Bucky Barnes aka The Winter Soldier, Daniel Brühl as Zemo, and Emily VanCamp as Sharon Carter.

On March 9, 2021, it was announced that The Falcon and The Winter Soldier will be streamed on Disney+ Hotstar dubbed in Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu languages. With this, it became the first Disney+ original series to be dubbed in the said languages.

On March 9, 2021, through a new TV spot for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, 15 seconds of new footage from this Marvel Studios' next Phase 4 release. What was included in this new footage happened to be a comedic scene at the end with Bucky falling through trees as Sam messes with him mentally through the use of his drone, Redwing. Also on this day, Kevin Feige in an interview went on to shower Anthony Mackie with praise over what he has managed to with the character of Sam. He also touched up on the feeling he and the other folks at Marvel Studios got when they settled on having Sam inherit the shield from Captain America.

On March 14, 2021, Kevin Feige was asked again at the press conference that took place on this day on whether a season 2 is already in the works. As far as a potential season 2, Feige simply said "If we’re able to do another one, there’s certainly ideas."

On March 15, 2021, Marvel Studios dropped the final trailer for the series. In this trailer, scenes featuring Bucky flirting with Sarah Wilson are shown, while also have some shirtless Sam scenes as well; Also on this day, a new image from The Falcon and The Winter Soldier teased a fiery Baron Zemo, who Daniel Brühl described as an "evolved" version in the Disney+ show.
On March 17, 2021, VanCamp said in a phone interview, that she first got the pitch for the show back in 2019.

On March 19, 2021, Spellman explained that the pandemic allowed the show's creative team to draw even more connectivity between the MCU and the current world people live in. Thus, when COVID hit and they got shut down, they were eventually able to actually, with a very light hand, draw even more connectivity between the MCU and the current world we all live in. In addition, Emily VanCamp revealed that she is returning to the Marvel Cinematic Universe as a "very, very different" Sharon Carter in The Falcon and The Winter Soldier; After the premiere of The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, currently, the show has a 93% after 106 reviews on Rotten Tomatoes. Unfortunately, the show's audience score is slightly lower, coming in at 79% after 383 reviews.
On March 22, 2021, a batch of merchandise for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier were released.

On March 22, 2021, addition merchandise for the show was released after the premiere of episode 1. On this same day, although they cited no concrete numbers, Disney Plus announced on Monday that "The Falcon and The Winter Soldier" was the streaming service's most-watched series premiere ever during its opening weekend, exceeding the series premieres for "The Mandalorian" and "WandaVision."; Speaking to USA Today, Russell explained in his interview that the main difference between the two Captain Americas is their upbringing and life experience. So U.S. Agent will have to grapple fitting into the moralistic superhero world and the mantle left behind by Captain America; St-Pierre teased that viewers can expect to see more of the guy known in the comics as "Batroc as the Leaper."

On March 23, 2021, new action figures from Hot Toys for the show were released. On this same day, a new look at Wyatt Russell's US Agent in The Falcon and The Winter Soldier was released ahead of the show's Friday premiere on Disney Plus two days later.

On April 5, 2021, Stan revealed in a radio interview on BBC Radio 1, that fans often spout the supposed code words that make his character of Bucky Barnes, a formerly brainwashed assassin, turn into a murder machine known as The Winter Soldier. These words being "Longing, rusted, seventeen, daybreak, furnace, nine, benign, homecoming, one, freight car," which were famously said by Zemo in Captain America: Civil War. Also on this day, new Funko Pop figures for Zemo and Sharon Carter as seen on episode 3 of The Falcon and The Winter Soldier were released.

On April 9, 2021, Toy maker Hasbro has put up for pre-order a brand new six-inch scale Marvel Legends figure from The Falcon and the Winter Soldier. The figure itself represents John Walker in his Captain America suit and features an interchangeable, unmasked head with the likeness of actor Wyatt Russell. On this same day, Daniel Brühl revealed that he actually improvised Zemo's dance moves that became a viral sensation since the airing of episode 3, Power Broker.
On April 12, 2021, after episode 4 The Whole World Is Watching aired, some additional merchandise for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier was released on the Marvel Entertainment store.

On April 23, 2021 Julia Louis-Dreyfus shared a 13-second video of herself as Contessa Valentina Allegra de Fontaine on the set of The Falcon and the Winter Soldier. She further revealed that in order to maintain the secrecy of her cameo, she wore a long black cloak with a full hood to hide her costume before she entered her first scene. Louis-Dreyfus took this precaution in stride, even joking in her post that she's "worn it every day since."

On April 24, 2021, during a recent interview with Vanity Fair, Wyatt Russell compared the teasing nature of the U.S. Agent reveal scene to that of a "carrot dangling in front of you. It was so much fun." Russell further admitted that he was less than excited about his new U.S. Agent suit, attributing this to the fact that both costumes were essentially the same: "When I went to see the costume, I thought there'd be a lot to deal with. It was…it's really the exact same costume but it's just black and red." He further added that his lackluster reaction worked well with his character during the scene where John Walker tells Val (Julia Louis-Dreyfus), "It's the same, but black." In addition, he said that "it provided a fun thing for me and Julia beyond what was on the page in that scene." Lastly, Russell also hinted at the future of the U.S. Agent in the MCU when he said that "at the end of the series, he's grown into himself in a very dangerous way."

On April 26, 2021, official promotional images have surfaced online, via Twitter user The Falcon and the Winter Soldier News and Marvel.com, of new Funko Pops for The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, including two versions of Sam Wilson as the new Captain America. In addition to a new Bucky Barnes Funko Pop, fans can now own a figure of Sam as Cap in his new, Wakanda-made Captain America suit holding the shield. As well a Funko Pop for John Walker in his US Agent suit too.

Following the announcement of Disney shifting physical media distribution to Sony Pictures Home Entertainment, this series, along with Moon Knight, are the last Marvel Studios presentations to be distributed by Walt Disney Studios Home Entertainment on physical media in North America.

The Fantastic Four: First Steps marks the introduction of the eponymous team and its two members: Invisible Woman, and Thing in the MCU. Both Mister Fantastic and Human Torch variants have appeared in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness and Deadpool & Wolverine respectively.
The Fantastic Four: First Steps also marks the introduction of H.E.R.B.I.E. from the Fantastic Four 1970's cartoons.

The Timely Comics office features comic book pages straight from the comics. They include appearances of Metallo (Tales of Suspense #16), Oog (Tales of Suspense #27), when the Fantastic Four fought Red Ghost and his super apes on the Blue Area of the moon and the debut of Uatu (Fantastic Four #13), Mister Fantastic entering the Negative Zone (Fantastic Four #51), and Thing and Human Torch in the Negative Zone (Fantastic Four Annual #6). They are all meant to pay tribute to Jack Kirby's work.

The Timely Comics office features a chalk board that reads "Big Unstoppable Monster!" This is likely a reference to early Tales of Suspense comics as well as some early issues of Journey into Mystery and Strange Tales comics that featured giant monsters. Those comics were made by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby in the late 1950s and 1960s, which is the same era Earth- 828 is in. It may also be a refence to Galactus being the main antagonist of the film.

The scene of the Timely Comics office may be a reference to Fantastic Four #10, the first time Stan Lee and Jack Kirby are shown working at Marvel. Their office has sketches of Hulk, Thor, and Ant-Man, and covers for Strange Tales, Tales to Astonish, and Tales of Suspense can be seen. Kirby is pitching a newly created villain, False-Face, when they are interrupted by the return of Doctor Doom who had been lost in space. Doctor Doom forced Lee and Kirby into trapping Mister Fantastic so that he could use body swapping technology he gained from the Ovoids since he had grown tired of wearing his mask and his scarred face.

At one point, it is theorized that Galactus could be a space dragon. This is likely a reference to the Makluans which are dragon-like aliens created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby in the Strange Tales comics. In the comics, they created what would become the Mandarin's Rings.

The scene of Igor stretching Reed's cheek from the credits was originally based on the cover of Fantastic Four Vol 7 22 by Alex Ross, where two Vampires are biting and stretching them. However, the final version of the scene that made it into credits is a bit different.

The post-credit scene featuring the The Fantastic Four Power Hour has the Fantastic Four running past a shop named Impossible Toys & Arcade, being a reference to Impossible Man and Arcade. The shop also has Arcade's signature yellow and red bow tie.

This film is the fifth live-action incarnation of the team, following two different sets of movies produced by 20th Century Fox, the one in Marvel Cinematic Universe film Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness and one in 1994. However, the 1994 movie was unreleased.
The cast of the 1994 film: Alex Hyde-White (Mister Fantastic), Jay Underwood (Human Torch), Rebecca Staab (Invisible Woman), and Michael Bailey Smith (Thing) make cameos in the movie.
Unlike all other MCU films, this movie has no connection to previous films and is the first film not to have any already established characters.
After saluting the street workers, the Human Torch uses his flames to make a 4 symbol in the sky, just like Chris Evans' Human Torch in the 2005 and 2007 films.

works.work: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special

facts.text: The Marvel Studios opening introduction is changed to comic panels and covers of Christmas issues.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Two films starring Kingo are visible when Mantis and Drax visit Hollywood including Haxan 3: Haxaner and Kingo's Kristmas.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Nebula gifts Rocket Bucky Barnes' Vibranium arm, a call back to Avengers: Infinity War when Rocket asked Barnes about his arm.

The Beverly Hills Police Department Officer Fitzgibbon is named after James Gunn's personal friend, Larry Fitzgibbon. Gunn puts a character named Fitzgibbon in all of his films. This is the third character named Fitzgibbon in the Marvel Cinematic Universe after Doctor Fitzgibbon from Guardians of the Galaxy and Officer Fitzgibbon from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2.
James Gunn pitched the idea of the holiday special to Kevin Feige while on the set of Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2.
This special was filmed alongside Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3.
This is the first Marvel Studios production to feature both live-action and 2D animation.
The Legends episodes prior to the holiday special, Drax and Mantis were taken down from Disney+ due to them spoiling the reveal that Mantis is Peter Quill's half-sister.
This is the only Guardians of the Galaxy project to not feature Zoe Saldaña (Gamora) in any capacity.

In the Bruce Jones Hulk comics, Betty Ross aided Bruce Banner as a shadowy contact under the alias "Mr. Blue". Mr. Blue appears in the film, but is revealed to be Samuel Sterns. The title Mr. Blue is also a reference to Tim Roth's crime film Reservoir Dogs, which featured Roth as Mr. Orange, and a Mr. Blue portrayed by Edward Bunker.
Betty Ross buys Bruce some purple pants. In the comics, Hulk is almost always seen wearing purple pants.

In the comics, the Abomination possesses pointed ears. Louis Leterrier wanted this characteristic to appear in the film, but reasoned that Hulk would bite them off (a la Mike Tyson on Evander Holyfield), which was considered too intense for a PG-13 film. The amphibian-like Abomination with pointed ears would first appear in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.

Tim Blake Nelson's character, Samuel Sterns, gets Hulk's blood in a wound in his head. His head starts to mutate and then he smiles. This is a foreshadowing of his role in a planned sequel as the villain, The Leader.
Hulk's origin in the Marvel Cinematic Universe is partially based on the Ultimate comics, where his transformation was the result of an attempt to recreate the Super Soldier Serum.

The Hulk's look was based on comic book artist Dale Keown's drawings, where "The Hulk, being beyond perfect, has zero grams of fat, is all chiselled, and is defined by his muscle and strength, so he's like a tank."

A label can be seen on the storage tank containing a serum vial reading: "Dr. Reinstein". Josef Reinstein was the alias of Abraham Erskine, the doctor who developed the Super Soldier Serum that transforms Steve Rogers into Captain America in the comics. The storage tank is marked "Weapons Plus". In the comics, the secret governmental program Weapon Plus purpose is the creation of super-soldiers intended to fight the wars of the future, especially a mutant-human war: Weapon I, also known as Project Rebirth, was responsible to transform Steve Rogers and Isaiah Bradley into super-soldiers; Weapon VI was responsible for giving Luke Cage his powers; and Weapon X experimented on Mutants, most notably Wolverine and Deadpool.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: S.H.I.E.L.D. appears twice in the movie: The names "Nick Fury" and S.H.I.E.L.D. appears on a government document, seen in the opening credits sequence; In the scene where Bruce Banner emails Mr. Blue with his data while Betty purchases the used truck, the email is tracked through the S.H.I.E.L.D. database.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: There are nods in the film to the then-upcoming film Captain America: The First Avenger. According to General Ross, the Super Soldier Serum was developed during World War II. Although cut from the theatrical run, Captain America can be seen in the alternate beginning on the DVD and Blu-ray. He is shown buried under the breaking ice after Banner's attempted suicide in the Arctic.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: A blueprint of the Sonic Cannon at Culver University appears in the opening credits sequence, bearing the title "Stark Industries", indicating that it was Tony Stark who built the cannons for General Ross to use against Hulk. Stark Industries also developed the Cryosync container storing the Super Soldier Serum created by Dr. Reinstein. The container also mentions Vita Radiation for the first time in the Marvel Cinematic Universe; The Iron Man 2 DVD Extras reveals that Stark Industries also created the Gamma Ray Projector.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Stark himself appears in the film's last scene and tells Thaddeus Ross that a team is being put together. As shown in Marvel One-Shot: The Consultant, Stark was in reality tasked as a consultant for S.H.I.E.L.D. with the mission to prevent General Thaddeus Ross from releasing Emil Blonsky onto the Avengers Initiative, as ordered by the World Security Council.

facts.section: References to the Incredible Hulk TV series
facts.text: The "Lonely Man" theme from the The Incredible Hulk TV series plays when Bruce Banner walks down the street in Mexico. Louis Ferrigno in The Incredible Hulk(2008) Lou Ferrigno's cameo.

facts.section: References to the Incredible Hulk TV series
facts.text: Three actors from previous Hulk television shows were in the film. Two were Paul Soles, who played Bruce Banner in the 1966 television show that aired on Tuesdays, playing the character Stanley Markowitz, and Lou Ferrigno, who played Hulk in the 1977–1982 The Incredible Hulk television series, playing a Culver University Security Guard and providing his voice for Hulk in the film. A scene from The Courtship of Eddie's Father shows the late Bill Bixby, who played Bruce Banner with Lou Ferrigno in the Incredible Hulk television series.

facts.section: References to the Incredible Hulk TV series
facts.text: Hulk's origin in the Marvel Cinematic Universe was partially based on David Banner, who was overexposed to gamma radiation on a Gamma Ray Projector.

facts.section: References to the Incredible Hulk TV series
facts.text: Betty Ross is a professor at Culver University, as the film suggests Bruce Banner had been prior to the experiment that turned him into Hulk. In the pilot for The Incredible Hulk television series, David Banner worked at The Culver Institute.

facts.section: References to the Incredible Hulk TV series
facts.text: After Hulk appears at Culver University, two students are interviewed in the news, named Jack McGee and Jim Wilson. Jack McGee was a tabloid reporter who attempted to track down Hulk in "The Incredible Hulk", and in the comics Jim Wilson was a young orphan who befriended Hulk.

facts.section: References to the Incredible Hulk TV series
facts.text: The package that Banner receives in British Columbia is addressed to "David B." This is a (very sly) reference to a key element of the 1970s television series, where the character's name was changed from Robert Bruce Banner to David Bruce Banner. Specifically, in his travels throughout the series, David would always maintain "David B." (e.g. David Benton, David Bishop) despite having to use a different name in every episode.

facts.section: References to the Incredible Hulk TV series
facts.text: The opening credits use the same X-ray shots of Banner's gamma irradiated skull, from the 1978 series. The '(D)ANGER' clip was reproduced from it as well. Also, Edward Norton's greenish-white eyes close up are eerily similar to Bill Bixby's.

Edward Norton, who had previously rewritten films he starred in, wrote a draft of the script which Louis Leterrier and Marvel Studios found satisfactory in establishing the film as a reboot of Hulk. As Norton explained, "I don't think that in great literature/films explaining the story's roots means it comes in the beginning. Audiences know the story, so we're dealing with it artfully." Norton's rewrite added the character of Leonard Samson and mentioned references to other Marvel Comics characters. He also wanted to put in "revelations about what set the whole thing in motion" that would be explained in future installments.

The VFX artists think of Blonsky as "a guy who transforms but is not used to having these new properties; for instance, he's much heavier, so when he walks down the sidewalk, he's tripping because his weight is destroying the sidewalk."
David Duchovny was a front-runner for the film before Edward Norton's casting as Bruce Banner. Dominic Purcell was rumored for the role as well.

The film joined Toronto's Green-Screen initiative, to help cut carbon emissions and waste created during filming. Hybrid and fuel-efficient vehicles were used, with low-sulphur diesel as their energy source. For constructing the sets, the production department used a sustainably-harvested locally sourced yellow pine, instead of the commonly-used lauan, and afterwards the wood was either recycled or given to environmental organizations. Paints with no/low volatile organic compounds were used, and paint cans were handed to waste management. A contractor was on set to remove bins. Environmentally-friendly items used on the set included cloth bags, biodegradable food containers, china and silverware food utensils, recycled paper, biodegradable soap and cleaners, rechargeable batteries and stainless steel mugs (one for each production member). Producer Gale Anne Hurd hopes the film will be a symbol of the drive to encourage less pollution from film productions.
Louis Leterrier had been interested in directing Iron Man, but when Jon Favreau took that project Avi Arad offered him a sequel to Hulk.

Tim Roth signed on the film because he was a fan of The Incredible Hulk television series, as well as to please his sons, who are comic book fan. On set, he constantly asked whether this would "be a cool shot" for his kids to see him in. He thoroughly enjoyed playing Blonsky, but found it difficult since to portray Blonsky's over-the-hill state he could not work out; but he hired a personal trainer to assist him in motion-capturing the Abomination's movements.
The VFX experts based Hulk and Abomination's movements on linebackers.

Louis Leterrier insisted Tim Roth, of whom he is a big fan, be cast as the film's main antagonist, even though Marvel Studios and Edward Norton were initially unsure of Roth as a supervillain. Leterrier later said "it's great watching a normal Cockney boy become a superhero!"

Edward Norton and Tim Roth filmed their Hulk-Abomination fracases on a stage, using motion capture and 37 digital cameras. Roth enjoyed using the motion capture technique because it reminded him of fringe theatre.
According to Tim Roth, Edward Norton rewrote scenes every day; Norton and Liv Tyler also spent hours discussing their characters' lives (especially before Hulk appeared).
William Hurt and his son are big fans of Hulk.

Although director Louis Leterrier liked Ang Lee's Hulk, he concurred with Marvel Studios that to continue the franchise it would be better to deviate from Lee's cerebral style from the first film and focus on a more action-filled tone. He also believed that in keeping with the poetic feel, the VFX were mostly "a fluorescent-green guy who was simply flying around; he had no weight and was too smooth-looking," so he wished to make the film's VFX grittier and darker "and perhaps even a little scarier!"

Hulk, as portrayed in this film, was created through a blend of motion capture and key frame animation (by Rhythm & Hues). In Ang Lee's movie, VFX were carried out by Industrial Light & Magic, with its director Ang Lee providing motion-capture.
Louis Leterrier directed four units with a broken foot.
It took the VFX artists over a year to construct a shot where Dr. Banner's gamma-irradiated blood falls through three factory stories into a bottle.
Paul Soles' character "Stanley Markowitz", the owner of the pizza shop, is a tribute to Hulk co-creator Stan Lee, as that is his real name.
Stan Lee has a cameo as the man who drinks the soft drink contaminated with Bruce Banner's blood.
According to screenwriter Zak Penn, this film was more similar to comic book writer Bruce Jones's Hulk concepts and The Incredible Hulk TV series.
Norton wrote a part specifically for Michael Kenneth Williams because he is a big fan of Williams' work on The Wire.

Hulk's look was based on comic book artist Dale Keown's drawings, where "Hulk, being beyond perfect, has zero grams of fat, is all chiseled, and is defined by his muscle and strength so he's like a tank."
According to Louis Leterrier, Hulk-out transformations in this film were inspired by An American Werewolf in London, where the change was shown as a painful process.

Visual effects supervisor Kurt Williams also created special computer programs that controlled the inflation of muscles and saturation of skin color for the transformations (since Williams reasoned that skin color was influenced by emotions, like blushing for instance).
In the opening credits, the name "Richard Jones" can be seen on a list of Banner's associates. Rick Jones served as Hulk's sidekick for many years. He appears in the video game tie-in.

In Germany the film was cut for a more commercial "Not under 12" rating. However, these cuts were done so clumsily that not only movie buffs but also average movie-goers noticed them, which resulted in lots of complaints to theater owners. To apologize for this, some cinemas gave away free movie tickets to the complaining customers. Additionally many cinemas, including some of Germany's largest cinema chains, included warning messages on their websites to raise awareness of the issue.

A scene where a futile Bruce Banner arrives at the Arctic to commit suicide was featured in the trailer, but was deemed too sensitive for young viewers and was removed from the film. This scene is mentioned in The Avengers.
William Hurt based his performance as General Ross on Captain Ahab, the obsessive captain who endlessly chased Moby Dick.

Edward Norton was cast as Bruce Banner on the recommendation of Lou Ferrigno, who had starred in The Incredible Hulk as Hulk. Ferrigno stated that Edward Norton reminded him of the late Bill Bixby, who acted beside him as Bruce Banner. Norton, who a big fan of the series, had also portrayed a similar character in Fight Club.
Stylistically, the filmmakers chose a darker shade of green from Hulk, and decided to not make him as large. His size does not increase as he becomes further enraged, staying at a consistent height.
Sam Elliott wanted to reprise his role as General Ross from Hulk, but it was taken by William Hurt.
The three-minute flashback that opens the film was created by editor Kyle Cooper.
Composer Craig Armstrong collaborated with Louis Leterrier to create the film's score. Marvel Studios were so pleased with the score they decided to release it as a two-disc soundtrack.
The sounds in the factory where Banner cuts himself are the same as the ones in the Carbonite chamber in Star Wars: Episode V - The Empire Strikes Back.

The Hercules aircraft (337) at the beginning of the movie is stationed at 8 Wing Trenton, Ontario Canada. It is a Canadian Air Force plane flown by Canadian Military pilots. It was painted to resemble the USAF planes.

There is a scene where Hulk smashes a police car in half, then wears both halves like boxing gloves. This is an ability taken directly from the video game The Incredible Hulk: Ultimate Destruction which was released for Gamecube, Xbox and PS2 in the summer of 2005.
The computer Edward Norton is using when he is disguised as a delivery boy has the virus scanner 'Norton' installed.
When Bruce is in Brazil the Jiu-Jitsu instructor that is teaching him to breathe is legendary Jiu-Jitsu Master Rickson Gracie.
In the final scene with Gen. Ross, he is drinking an "Incredible Hulk" cocktail at the bar. It is made using equal parts Hennessy cognac and Hpnotiq liqueur.

The film is a "reboot" of the Hulk franchise, not a sequel to Hulk. Lou Ferrigno, who has made a cameo as a security guard in both, is the only actor who reprises his role from Ang Lee's film. Stan Lee also has small cameos in both films. In Hulk as a security guard talking to Lou Ferrigno in the same scene Ferrigno cameos in and in the Incredible Hulk as a man who drinks the soft drink contaminated with Bruce Banner's blood.

In 2003, James Schamus had written a treatment for a direct sequel to Hulk featuring the Grey Hulk with The Leader and The Abomination under consideration as the lead villain. However, Universal at that time owns the rights to making the film and by the time the rights expired at the end of 2005, Marvel's own studio bought back the rights of making the movie with Universal only distributing it.

Edward Norton rewrote the script substantially and in certain posters, he was credited under the pseudonym of 'Edward Harrison'. Norton's writing credit was later denied by the WGA, and Zak Penn is the only writer credited.

The Incredible Hulk is the only of the four films released in the summer of 2008, based on a comic book, that wasn't nominated for any Academy Awards. (The others being The Dark Knight, Iron Man and Hellboy II: The Golden Army.)
The final fight scene between Hulk and Abomination was filmed in Toronto, Canada. The beginning of the fight is filmed outside of the Zanzibar strip club on Yonge street.
William Hurt was under consideration for the role of Gen. Robert E. Lee in Gettysburg. Another role, that of Gen. John Buford, ended up being played by Sam Elliott, who played General Ross in Hulk.

Two years prior to taking the role of Bruce Banner, Edward Norton had the lead role in The Illusionist. Three years before Bill Bixby gave his performance of Banner in The Incredible Hulk TV series, he had the lead in television series The Magician.

In the comics, Emil Blonsky takes on a scaly reptilian appearance, becoming the Abomination. Louis Leterrier felt that while that was cool, it made no sense considering there was no reptile in his origin. In this film Blonsky's appearance is redefined substantially to have his skin/muscles/bones exaggerated and sticking out all over his body. Leterrier describes Blonsky as "an über-human, just like Hulk, but a human who was injected with something in the wrong places and these places are growing differently." The VFX artists think of Blonsky as "a guy who transforms but is not used to having these new properties; for instance, he's much heavier, so when he walks down the sidewalk, he's tripping because his weight is destroying the sidewalk."

According to Louis Leterrier, the final scene (Banner grins as his eyes turn green) was a deliberately ambiguous shot: it was meant to show that Bruce finally learns to controls Hulk (for a Hulk sequel) or will become a menace (as the villain for the film The Avengers). Neither of which has happened, but Hulk did attack the Helicarrier in The Avengers.

Although the final scenes are set in Harlem, they were shot in Toronto, with the initial showdown between Hulk and the Abomination being filmed on Yonge Street. Several Toronto icons are visible, most notably the "spinning disc" sign for Sam the Record Man, and the marquee of the Zanzibar Tavern.
Hulk has a total of six words: "Leave Me Alone", "Hulk Smash", and "Betty".
This is the first film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe that doesn't have a post-credit scene.

This is the only pre-2012 Marvel Studios production that was not distributed by Paramount Pictures. Instead Universal Pictures (which produced the previous Hulk film) was left in charge of distribution.
The Incredible Hulk is the only movie from Phase One that did not have a direct sequel in Phase Two, and the only one to feature Bruce Banner as the main hero.

In the shot of the Pentagon, Theodore Roosevelt Island can be seen. There is no sign of the Triskelion, despite the fact that the Triskelion was constructed in the 1980s, and the film takes place in the early 21st century.

The reckless taxi ridden by Betty and Bruce on their way to meet Sterns (body number 57Q0) later runs into Abomination. The cab, along with the driver, is promptly used to smash over some soldiers right after the Abomination bellows his hunger for a real fight.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The scene of Kamala Khan recruiting Kate Bishop is an allusion to Nick Fury recruiting Tony Stark in the post-credit scene of Iron Man. During the scene, Khan indirectly mentions Cassie Lang, saying Ant-Man had a daughter.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Emperor Dro'ge and his colony on Tarnax IV are featured within the film, having been previously mentioned in Secret Invasion as the only colony of Skrulls not on Earth.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: The film contains flashbacks to the events of the Westview Anomaly, featured in WandaVision.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
facts.text: Having previously promised to go after the Supreme Intelligence in Captain Marvel, the film includes flashbacks to Carol Danvers destroying the Supreme Intelligence.
The S.A.B.E.R. Space Station resembles the Peak VII from the comics.
In the comics, Aladna is a planet where the residents speaks in rhyme. In order to translate this into live-action, the Aladneans have a language of Song.
The Marvels introduces Dar-Benn, an accuser from the comics who has been gender swapped in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
Kelsey Grammer reprises his role as Beast, having portrayed an alternate version of the character in the 20th Century Fox productions X-Men: The Last Stand and X-Men: Days of Future Past.
The Marvels has been delayed four times.
The production title for The Marvels was Goat Rodeo.
S.A.B.E.R. is an original organization for the Marvel Cinematic Universe which does not exist in Marvel comics.

Following the announcement of Disney shifting physical media distribution to Sony Pictures Home Entertainment, this is the last Marvel Studios feature film to be distributed by Walt Disney Studios Home Entertainment on physical media in North America.
The Marvels is the first MCU sequel whose title does not consist of the original film's title followed by a number (ex. Iron Man 2) or subtitle (ex. Captain America: The Winter Soldier).
The Marvels is the first MCU film to have a character introduced within a television series as a lead character, that being Ms. Marvel, who co-leads alongside Monica Rambeau and Captain Marvel.

The Marvels, at 105 minutes runtime, is the shortest movie in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. This was Director Nia DaCosta's longest runtime for a film at the time of release, until 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple in 2026, at 109 minutes. DaCosta, when asked about the runtime, explained that she felt like she did what was right for the movie, and had wanted it to be under two hours.

Barbra Streisand's cover of the song "Memory" that played while the Flerkens, a species with a visual resemblance to cats, swallowed the S.A.B.E.R. crew members, previously served as the emotional climax of the musical Cats. Director Nia DaCosta called it her proudest moment in directing.
Originally, a different needle drop from another Black artist was planned for during the Destruction of Tarnax IV, before they settled on the song "RATATA".

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe / Movies and TV Shows
facts.text: Micro was previously mentioned in the Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. episode The Writing on the Wall and the Daredevil episode A Cold Day in Hell's Kitchen.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe / Movies and TV Shows
facts.text: The Dogs of Hell make an appearance, after appearing in both Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Daredevil.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe / Movies and TV Shows
facts.text: WHiH World News, a recurring news network in the Marvel Cinematic Universe movies and television series, is featured.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe / Movies and TV Shows
facts.text: NY1 reporter Pat Kiernan was previously featured in The Avengers, Iron Man 3, Doctor Strange and Daredevil.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe / Movies and TV Shows
facts.text: The Duel of Harlem from The Incredible Hulk and the Battle of New York from The Avengers are both seen on newspapers.

facts.section: References to the Marvel Cinematic Universe / Movies and TV Shows
facts.text: O'Harren's Scotch Whisky is used in the show after previously appearing in Agent Carter and Daredevil.
